title: REST client never sends Authorization; SPA unusable with auth-enabled API
root_cause: Every page uses lib/api.ts whose requestEnvelope sends only Content-Type. The token-aware client (api/client.ts, reads localStorage 'loop.token') is used only for WebSocket URLs, never REST. No login flow exists to obtain a token even though the API exposes POST /api/v1/auth/login and LOOP_REQUIRE_AUTH enforcement (config default false; supported deployment mode).
suggested_fix: Route all REST calls through a token-aware client, add a login screen storing the JWT (in memory), handle 401 by redirecting to login.
failure_scenario: Operator deploys with LOOP_REQUIRE_AUTH=true: every list/load/save returns 401; Dashboard, Workflows, Editor, Executions all error with no way to log in.
verification_notes: lib/api.ts requestEnvelope now attaches Authorization: Bearer from localStorage loop.token (same key the WS client uses); 401 clears the token and redirects to /login (auth routes exempt to avoid loops); added api.login() and pages/Login.tsx wired at /login in App.tsx. No token -> no header, so auth-disabled deployments unchanged. Regression: tests/unit/canvas/api-auth.test.ts (4 cases). Verified: npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/canvas/tsconfig.json exit 0; turbo build canvas succeeds; pnpm test:unit 683/683; eslint 0 errors (new files carry only the systemic import/order resolver warnings). Note: token in localStorage matches existing WS client convention; hardening to in-memory/cookie is a follow-up (see #23).

title: addNode derives ID from nodes.length; delete+add creates duplicate IDs
root_cause: nodeId = `node_${nodes.length + 1}`. After deleting any node (or loading a graph whose IDs are not contiguous node_1..N), the next added node reuses an existing ID. Node IDs are not editable in the UI; the server validator rejects duplicate IDs on PUT.
suggested_fix: Generate IDs from a monotonic counter/max existing suffix or crypto.randomUUID(), checking against current node IDs.
failure_scenario: Open a template with node_1..node_5, delete node_2, add a palette node -> named node_5 (duplicate). React Flow renders two nodes with one key, edges bind ambiguously, every Save fails with 'duplicate node ID(s)' — graph unsavable and unfixable from the UI.
verification_notes: addNode now uses nextNodeId(existing ids) (max node_N suffix + 1) via new pure helper apps/canvas/src/lib/graph.ts; useCallback deps updated to [nodes]. Regression: tests/unit/canvas/graph.test.ts (delete+add, non-contiguous, custom ids, never-collides). Verified: canvas tsc 0; canvas build OK; unit 683/683; eslint 0 errors.

title: Save strips retry, timeout_ms, schemas and workflow settings from definition
root_cause: toRfNode keeps only id/type/position/config and buildDefinition rebuilds nodes/edges from scratch, dropping WorkflowNode.retry, timeout_ms, input_schema, output_schema, edge.type_compatibility and definition.settings (workflow_timeout_ms). Server zod defaults silently re-default type_compatibility to true. 16 of 23 shipped templates contain retry/timeout/settings blocks.
suggested_fix: Carry original WorkflowNode/edge objects in node/edge data and spread unknown fields back on save; preserve definition.settings.
failure_scenario: Instantiate 'invoice-approval' (nodes carry retry/timeout_ms), change one label, Save: all retry policies, per-node timeouts and workflow timeout silently erased; flaky connector calls now fail the whole run instead of retrying.
verification_notes: toRfNode/toRfEdge stash the original node/edge in data.original; buildDefinition delegates to buildDefinitionFromGraph (lib/graph.ts) which spreads originals back (retry, timeout_ms, schemas, edge.type_compatibility) and preserves definition.settings; canvas WorkflowDefinition type gained settings. Regression: tests/unit/canvas/graph.test.ts round-trip (edited config/position applied; retry/timeout/settings/type_compatibility preserved; new nodes plain). Verified: canvas tsc 0; canvas build OK; unit 683/683; eslint 0 errors.

suggested_fix: Add COPY --from=builder lines for packages/templates/dist and packages/templates/package.json (plus the templates/*.json data directory — separate finding).

Verified: pnpm exec turbo run build --filter=@loop/templates... succeeds (dist/index.js produced); pnpm typecheck exit 0; pnpm test:unit 664/664 pass. docker CLI unavailable locally; image build verified statically + CI docker-build step.

title: Sandbox image runs 'node src/server.ts' with no build and no deps
root_cause: CMD executes TypeScript source directly. Image never runs tsc, never installs node_modules (fastify etc.); base python:3.11-slim + apt nodejs (Debian node 18; nodesource setup on line 9 only adds a repo and is '|| true') cannot execute .ts. apps/sandbox has only src/server.ts in git.
suggested_fix: Use a node:20 builder stage that installs deps and builds (like Dockerfile.controlplane), run dist/server.js, drop the curl|bash nodesource step.
failure_scenario: loop-sandbox container exits immediately (SyntaxError/ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND). docker-compose.yml gates loop-app on service_healthy for loop-sandbox, so the whole Core-tier compose deployment never starts. Same broken image pushed to ghcr.io by release.yml.

Verified: turbo build 6/6 tasks succeed, dist/server.js exists; server listens on LOOP_SANDBOX_PORT (compose sets 4000) with /health; compose healthcheck uses busybox wget present in alpine. docker build deferred to CI.

title: IPv6 private-range check misses non-canonical loopback/v4-mapped forms
root_cause: isPrivateIPv6() compares strings against '::1'/'::' and a dotted-decimal v4-mapped regex only. '0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1' (expanded loopback) fails equality; first label '0' parses to 0x0000 (not fc00/fe80) -> false. '::ffff:7f00:1' (hex v4-mapped 127.0.0.1) fails the dotted regex; first label '' -> returns false at line 59. isIP() accepts both as valid IPv6, so firstPrivateAddress (93) takes the literal path and returns null -> EgressGate.check allows the URL even with allowPrivate=false (the config default).
suggested_fix: Parse IPv6 literals into 16 bytes (expand :: and groups) and evaluate ranges numerically: ::1/128, ::/128, fc00::/7, fe80::/10, ::ffff:0:0/96 with embedded IPv4 run through isPrivateIPv4. Never rely on string forms.
failure_scenario: With LOOP_EGRESS_ALLOW_PRIVATE=false (default), a generic.rest_call node targeting http://[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]:3000/ or http://[::ffff:7f00:1]:3000/ passes the gate and undici connects to the API's own loopback listener / internal services — the exact SSRF the blocklist claims to stop.
verification_notes: isPrivateIPv6 now parses literals into 16 bytes (parseIPv6Bytes handles :: compression + dotted-IPv4 tails) and evaluates ::1/128, ::/128, ::ffff:0:0/96 (embedded IPv4), fc00::/7, fe80::/10 numerically. Regression: private-blocklist.test.ts audit #7 cases (expanded loopback, hex v4-mapped, gate-level URL checks). Verified: pnpm typecheck 0; pnpm test:unit 672/672 (51 files); pnpm test:integration 168/169 (pre-existing vault multipart failure only); eslint 0 errors, warnings = baseline + systemic import/order on new test file.

title: DNS rebinding TOCTOU between egress check and actual connection
root_cause: firstPrivateAddress() resolves the host via dns.lookup (getaddrinfo), then EgressGate.check returns and the adapter calls undici request(), which resolves the hostname again independently at connect time. The resolved-and-validated IP is never pinned to the connection; Node performs a fresh lookup per call.
suggested_fix: Resolve once, validate all answers, then connect to the validated IP (custom undici Agent connect/lookup returning the pinned address, or request by IP with explicit Host header). Re-validate at connect time rather than only at check time.
failure_scenario: Attacker-controlled authoritative DNS with TTL=0 alternates A records: public IP during the gate's lookup, 127.0.0.1/169.254.169.254 during undici's connect lookup. A workflow node pointing at rebinding.attacker.tld passes the private-address blocklist and reaches cloud metadata or internal services despite allowPrivate=false.
verification_notes: Skipped this round: a correct fix must pin the validated IP to the actual connection (custom undici Agent connect/lookup or connect-time re-validation) across ALL adapters (vault/desk/recap/generic/llm providers) — a cross-cutting connection-layer design change too risky for a minimal-edit batch. Recommended design: shared egress-safe undici dispatcher in @loop/egress whose lookup hook resolves+validates at connect time (fail-closed), injected via ExecuteParams. Needs design review. NOT fixed — remains open.

title: Pruned-node rows collide with idempotency unique index on resume/replay
root_cause: pruneInactiveNodes unconditionally calls nodeExecutions.create with stable idempotency_key `${executionId}:${node.id}` for every branch-skipped node, without the findByIdempotencyKey reuse guard executeNodeInner (592-631) applies. Unique index idx_node_exec_idem (state migrations/index.ts:184, migrations-pg.ts:181) rejects a second insert for the same key.
suggested_fix: In pruneInactiveNodes look up findByIdempotencyKey first; if a row exists (e.g. 'skipped' from the prior attempt) reuse it / treat as idempotent hit instead of inserting.
failure_scenario: control.branch workflow: false-arm node gets a 'skipped' row, execution fails or process crashes. Recovery resume (or POST /executions/:id/replay?dryRun=false) restores the branch decision, prunes the same node again, create() throws UNIQUE constraint, executeInner catch marks execution 'failed'. Any execution with branch-skipped nodes can never be resumed or non-dry replayed.
verification_notes: pruneInactiveNodes now looks up findByIdempotencyKey and reuses the prior skipped row instead of re-inserting (mirrors executeNodeInner guard). Regression: tests/unit/engine/executor-branch.test.ts audit #9 (fail-then-resume branch workflow). Verified: pnpm typecheck exit 0; pnpm test:unit 667/667; pnpm test:integration 168/169 (only pre-existing vault multipart failure); eslint changed files 0 errors / 10 warnings = baseline.

title: Workflow timeout between levels/batches marks execution 'succeeded'
root_cause: executeLevel breaks out of the batch loop when signal.aborted without producing any rejected result; executeInner (311-333) only fails on a rejected settled result and never checks workflowTimedOut/signal.aborted after the level loop. If the workflow timer fires while no node is in flight (during getById/prune awaits or between batches), every remaining level returns an empty settled array and the run completes 'succeeded'. TSD §6.1 requires timeout to mark failed.
suggested_fix: After each executeLevel (and after the level loop) check controller.signal.aborted/workflowTimedOut and throw WORKFLOW_TIMEOUT; or have executeLevel return a rejected result for unscheduled nodes when aborted.
failure_scenario: workflow_timeout_ms=1000; level-1 node finishes at 900ms; timer fires at 1000ms during level-2 store reads/pruning. Levels 2..N break immediately with settled=[], no failure found, completeExecution writes 'succeeded' and execution_succeeded recorded although most nodes never ran — silent partial execution reported as success.
verification_notes: executeInner now throws WORKFLOW_TIMEOUT when controller.signal.aborted after each executeLevel, covering deadlines firing between levels/batches. Regression: tests/unit/engine/executor-resume.test.ts audit #10 (delayed second per-level store read). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 667/667; integration 168/169 (pre-existing failure only); eslint 0 new errors/warnings.

title: Sub-workflow retry/resume creates fresh child execution, re-firing side effects
root_cause: invokeSubWorkflow generates childExecutionId = randomUUID() on every invocation. executeWithRetry (default LOOP_DEFAULT_RETRY_COUNT=3 wired in server.ts) re-invokes dispatchNode on child failure, and parent resume re-invokes the node; each attempt gets a brand-new child execution id, so the child's completedOutputs/idempotency keys never match prior attempts and every child node re-dispatches.
suggested_fix: Derive child execution id deterministically from the parent idempotency key (UUIDv5 of `${executionId}:${node.id}`) or look up an existing child execution by parent node key, so retries/resume reuse the child's succeeded-node skip path.
failure_scenario: workflow.invoke node: child node A performs a POST (side effect, row succeeded), child node B fails transiently. Retry -> new child execution id -> A's idempotency key differs -> POST fires again. Same duplication when parent crashes after child completed but before parent node row marked succeeded and recovery resumes.
verification_notes: Child execution id now deterministic UUIDv5 of parentExecutionId:nodeId (subWorkflowExecutionId helper); existing child row reused so retry/resume skips succeeded child nodes. Regression: tests/unit/engine/executor-subworkflow.test.ts audit #11 (invoke retry fires child side effect exactly once; single child row). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 667/667; integration 168/169 (pre-existing failure only); eslint 0 new errors/warnings.

title: Scoped secret upsert collides with globally-unique secret name
root_cause: set() looks up by (name, scope, scope_id) and INSERTs when no row matches, but secrets.name is globally UNIQUE in both tiers (schema.ts:148 .unique(); migrations-pg.ts:124 UNIQUE). A second distinct scope_id with the same name finds no matching row and the insert violates UNIQUE(name). POST /api/v1/connectors (routes/index.ts:646) stores every connector key under name 'api_key'; server.ts:186 migration does the same.
suggested_fix: Make uniqueness composite (name, scope, scope_id) in both stores and match scope_id exactly (including NULL) in getByName; or namespace stored names per scope_id. Delete connector-scoped secrets on DELETE /connectors.
failure_scenario: Create connector A with api_key (OK) -> create connector B with api_key -> set('api_key','connector',B) finds no row -> INSERT -> UNIQUE violation -> 409; no second keyed connector can ever be created via the API. Startup migration silently keeps plaintext for every legacy row after the first (server.ts:197-199). Deleting connector A orphans its 'api_key' row, permanently blocking future keyed connector creation.
verification_notes: Migration 003 in both stores: SQLite rebuilds secrets without inline UNIQUE(name); PG drops secrets_name_key; both add unique index (name, scope, COALESCE(scope_id, empty-string)) so NULL scope_id folds into one comparable value. drizzle schema.ts .unique() removed. Regression: tests/unit/secrets/manager.test.ts (two connectors each store api_key; same-scope upsert; global+workflow coexist). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 672/672; integration 168/169 (pre-existing only; state/migration suite passes with 003). PG migration verified statically (no local PG). Orphaned connector-scoped rows after DELETE no longer block creation (composite key).

title: Airgap E2E never enables airgap; 'local LLM' node is a no-network mock
root_cause: Neither test sets LOOP_AIRGAP_MODE or constructs an EgressGate. Test 1 inserts deny policies and calls egressEngine.evaluate directly; test 2 runs createMockAdapter('local_llm') performing zero HTTP through an executor with no gate (tests/e2e/helpers.ts:134). Header comment 'airgap check not yet wired into connectors' is stale — production wires it (server.ts:127-131,237).
suggested_fix: Build the context with EgressGate({airgap:true}) passed to the executor, register an adapter making a real HTTP call to a loopback mock server, assert execution fails NODE_EGRESS_BLOCKED; assert localhost-allow succeeds only with airgap off.
failure_scenario: Airgap leaking on the workflow execution path (gate dropped from executor wiring, adapter ignoring params.egress) ships green under a suite named 'Air-gapped deployment mode (E2E)' — data sovereignty is the product's first-class constraint.
verification_notes: Rewrote tests/e2e/airgapped-deployment.test.ts: kept the engine-level deny test; replaced the no-network mock test with two real-path tests wiring EgressGate({airgap}) into ExecutionExecutor and driving the REAL GenericAdapter against a loopback node:http server. Airgap on: execution fails NODE_EGRESS_BLOCKED and server receives 0 requests; airgap off (allowPrivate): execution succeeds and server receives exactly /probe. Stale header comment removed. Verified: typecheck 0; unit 673/673; integration 171/172 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30; eslint 0 errors.

title: Test executor built without egress gate, secret resolver, or config timeouts
root_cause: buildTestApp constructs new ExecutionExecutor(store, connectors, 10) while production (apps/api/src/server.ts:223-249) passes executionEventBus, eventOutputMaxBytes, egressGate, secretResolver and retry config. In the test app egressGate/secretResolver are undefined; dispatchNode only forwards egress when the gate exists and adapters fail open (await io?.egress?.check(url)). Helper LOOP_NODE_TIMEOUT_MS/LOOP_WORKFLOW_TIMEOUT_MS/LOOP_MAX_CONCURRENT are dead. No test in the repo constructs ExecutionExecutor with a real egressGate. See also the unit-suite finding on executor-branch.test.ts.
suggested_fix: Wire the helper executor exactly like server.ts (egressGate, secretResolver, eventBus, eventOutputMaxBytes, retry). Add an integration test running a workflow whose connector targets a denied domain asserting NODE_EGRESS_BLOCKED, plus one proving connector api_key reaches the adapter via the secrets store.

Secrets-resolution regressions in the API path are likewise invisible.
verification_notes: buildTestApp now constructs ExecutionExecutor with production parity (server.ts order): LOOP_MAX_CONCURRENT, LOOP_NODE_TIMEOUT_MS, LOOP_WORKFLOW_TIMEOUT_MS, executionEventBus, eventOutputMaxBytes, egressGate, secretResolver (secretsManager.get), default retry from config. Verified: pnpm typecheck 0; pnpm test:unit 673/673; pnpm test:integration 171/172 (only pre-existing vault multipart failure); pnpm test:e2e 30/30; eslint changed files 0 errors, warnings <= baseline.

title: No test pins executor->adapter egress gate wiring; airgap can silently die
root_cause: Every executor test constructs ExecutionExecutor without an egressGate (this file passes undefined explicitly). No unit test builds the executor WITH a gate and asserts adapter.execute receives egress or that check() runs. The wiring is one spread at executor.ts:836 and every adapter consults it via optional chaining (params.egress?.check), so a missing gate fails OPEN silently. Companion structural gap: tests/integration/_helpers/app.ts finding.
suggested_fix: Add an executor test: recording adapter + stub gate whose check rejects; execute a connector node; assert adapter received the gate, check called with target URL, node fails NODE_EGRESS_BLOCKED. Also assert airgap=true blocks generic.rest_call end-to-end.
failure_scenario: A refactor drops the egress spread (or renames the param): LOOP_AIRGAP_MODE, all egress policies and the SSRF private blocklist become dead config for every connector node — the exact bug the S1 wiring fix addressed — and the entire unit suite stays green.
verification_notes: Added tests/unit/engine/executor-branch.test.ts audit #15: executor constructed WITH a denying gate (9th arg); asserts adapter received the gate instance, check() consulted, node/execution fail with the egress error. A dropped egress spread now fails this test. Verified: typecheck 0; unit 673/673; integration 171/172 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30.

title: API replay guards (REPLAY_IN_PROGRESS / REPLAY_NOT_TERMINAL) untested
root_cause: replay.test.ts covers replayExecution/computeReplayDecisions only. Route-level guards (routes/index.ts:385-427: in-flight Set -> 409 REPLAY_IN_PROGRESS; non-terminal status -> 409 REPLAY_NOT_TERMINAL; dryRun default query['dryRun'] !== 'false') have zero matches anywhere under tests/ (grep-verified).
suggested_fix: Add route-level tests (Fastify inject with real route registration): two concurrent POST /executions/:id/replay?dryRun=false -> second 409 REPLAY_IN_PROGRESS; dryRun=false on running/pending/paused -> 409 REPLAY_NOT_TERMINAL and no dispatch; POST with no query param defaults to dry-run (no side effects).
failure_scenario: A regression removes the Set guard or inverts the dryRun default: concurrent replays double-fire connector side effects (duplicate emails, double Vault/Desk writes), or a default POST re-executes a running workflow. Nothing in the suite fails.
verification_notes: Added two route-level tests in tests/integration/api/replay.test.ts: (1) POST ?dryRun=false on running execution -> 409 REPLAY_NOT_TERMINAL; (2) concurrent replays via a hanging adapter -> second POST 409 REPLAY_IN_PROGRESS, first completes 200. Default dry-run was already covered. Verified: typecheck 0; unit 673/673; integration 171/172 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30.

title: JWT accepted without rechecking user status; 12h hard-coded life
root_cause: resolveIdentity() trusts any signature-valid JWT's sub/role claims and never consults users.is_active or existence. routes/auth.ts:118 hard-codes 12-hour expiry (ignoring LOOP_JWT_ACCESS_TTL); no revocation mechanism. Store supports deactivation (sqlite/index.ts:523) but it has no effect on already-issued tokens.
suggested_fix: On each authenticated request (or via short access TTL + revocation list) verify the user still exists and is_active; honour LOOP_JWT_ACCESS_TTL for issued tokens.
failure_scenario: Operator deactivates a compromised editor account -> previously issued JWT keeps passing the guard with editor role for up to 12 more hours, continuing to create/execute workflows and read data.

title: PUT /triggers returns webhook signing secret unredacted
root_cause: GET /workflows/:id/triggers maps redactTriggerSecrets (529) and the comment states secrets never leave the API, but PUT /api/v1/triggers/:triggerId returns the raw store row including config.secret. POST create intentionally returns the secret once; PUT re-exposes it on every update.
suggested_fix: Apply redactTriggerSecrets to the PUT response (521) as done for the GET list.
failure_scenario: Editor (requiredRoleFor gives editor for PUT) sends PUT /api/v1/triggers/<webhook-trigger> {enabled:true} -> response contains config.secret in cleartext -> editor can forge correctly-signed webhook payloads to the public /webhooks/:triggerId endpoint, impersonating the external system.
verification_notes: PUT /api/v1/triggers/:triggerId now applies redactTriggerSecrets to the response (parity with GET list). Regression: trigger-to-execution.test.ts audit #18 (PUT returns ***redacted***). Verified: pnpm typecheck 0; unit 685/685; integration 174/175 (pre-existing vault multipart failure only); e2e 30/30; eslint delta 0.

title: Connector header credentials stored plaintext; migration gap
root_cause: POST /connectors extracts only api_key into the encrypted secrets store; config.headers (e.g. authorization) remains plaintext in connectors.config JSON. server.ts:174-176 comment claims the L-2 migration moves 'api_key (and headers.authorization)' into the encrypted store, but migration code (182-200) only handles api_key. GET redaction hides headers from API reads but the live credential stays unencrypted at rest.
suggested_fix: Extract sensitive header values into the secrets store on create and in the startup migration (resolve at dispatch like api_key), or encrypt the whole config column; align migration with its comment.
failure_scenario: Editor creates a generic connector with config.headers.authorization='Bearer <live token>' -> token persisted as plaintext JSON in SQLite/PG -> anyone with DB/file access (backups, snapshots) reads the upstream credential, violating the encryption-at-rest guarantee the L-2 work claims.

title: Forced LLM provider silently falls back to cloud vendors
root_cause: When body.provider is set the route builds chain=[provider, ...every other configured vendor] and the router (llm/router.ts:37-76) tries each in order on ANY failure — including an egress block. With default LOOP_EGRESS_ALLOW_PRIVATE=false (config.ts:172) the local Ollama URL (localhost:11434) is always blocked by the private-address gate, so the 'forced' local provider deterministically fails over to cloud vendors.
suggested_fix: When provider explicitly specified pass chain=[body.provider] only (no fallback), or require an explicit allow_fallback flag; surface the egress block as the error instead of switching vendors.
failure_scenario: Deployment with Ollama + OpenAI key configured; caller POSTs /api/v1/llm/complete {provider:'ollama',prompt:'<confidential data>'} expecting local-only processing -> gate blocks localhost -> router sends the prompt to api.openai.com -> confidential data leaves the sovereign boundary contrary to the explicit provider choice.
verification_notes: Forced provider chain is now exclusive: chain=[body.provider] (unknown provider still 400 via existing validation). Regression: router.test.ts audit #20 (explicit chain does not fall through to cloud vendor on failure). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 685/685; integration 174/175 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30; eslint delta 0.

title: Recovery/cron/webhook dispatch resumes with LIVE definition, not version snapshot
root_cause: dispatchToExecutor loads authoring.getById(workflowId) (live current definition) instead of resolving the execution's stamped workflow_version snapshot. A workflow edited between crash and restart resumes against a different graph while loadCompletedOutputs seeds outputs from the old version's nodes; cron/webhook executions can likewise run a newer version than stamped on the execution row. Engine-side replay.ts resolveDefinition is versioned and correct — the gap is in the injected dispatcher (verified during cross-pass review).
suggested_fix: Resolve the definition via the execution's workflow_version (workflowDefinitions.getByWorkflowAndVersion, falling back explicitly and logging when absent) before executor.execute; stamp-and-resolve consistently on all dispatch paths.
failure_scenario: Execution of workflow v3 crashes mid-run; operator edits the workflow to v4 (renames/removes nodes); restart resumes the v3 execution against the v4 graph — seeded outputs reference nodes that no longer exist, branch decisions misalign, and the audit trail claims v3 while v4 ran.

title: /ready hardcodes database 'ok' and always returns HTTP 200
root_cause: Readiness handler performs no database probe — checks.database is the literal 'ok' — and returns status:'ready' with HTTP 200 even when connectorsOk is false ('degraded'). Readiness reports ready regardless of actual dependency health. (Egress bypass on the same probe path is covered under the connectors healthCheck finding.)
suggested_fix: Probe the store (trivial query) and return 503 with status:'not_ready' when DB or required connectors are down.
failure_scenario: SQLite file corrupted / PG connection lost after startup -> /ready still answers 200 {database:'ok'} -> load balancer/k8s keeps routing traffic to an instance where every request 500s.
verification_notes: /ready now probes the store (workflows.list page 1) and returns 503 not_ready when DB or connectors are down; database check reflects reality. buildTestApp also registers /ready for production parity. Regression: admin-routes.test.ts audit #22 (200 healthy; 503 with store.list rejecting). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 685/685; integration 174/175 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30; eslint delta 0.

title: Bearer token sent as WS URL query param; leaked into access logs
root_cause: buildExecutionWsUrl appends ?token=<JWT/API key>. Fastify request logging and intermediary proxies record full URLs including query strings, persisting credentials in plaintext logs (CWE-598).
suggested_fix: Use a short-lived single-use ticket exchanged over REST, or Sec-WebSocket-Protocol carrier; at minimum redact token from server URL logging.
failure_scenario: Auth-enforced deployment: a viewer opens an execution monitor; their JWT is written to API/proxy access logs. Anyone with log read access can replay the token until expiry.

title: Only 'branch' renders named handles; control.condition port edges invisible
root_cause: ControlNode renders true/false source handles only for controlType==='branch'; other control types get a single unnamed handle. toRfEdge (WorkflowEditor.tsx:84) maps any source_port != 'output' to a named sourceHandle, so edges from control.condition nodes (e.g. 'auto_approve'/'needs_review' in templates/content-review-pipeline.json) reference nonexistent handles and React Flow drops them.
suggested_fix: Render a source handle per configured outgoing port for all control node types.
failure_scenario: Instantiate 'content-review-pipeline': the condition node's outgoing edges are invisible ('couldn't create edge' warning); graph looks disconnected, user cannot see or rewire routing.

title: Terminal WS event ignores durationMs; Duration stays '—' forever
root_cause: applyStreamEvent sets status from execution_succeeded/execution_failed but discards event.durationMs and never sets completed_at. The 4s poll (128-132) stops once status is terminal, so duration_ms remains the null captured at load.
suggested_fix: On terminal events set duration_ms: event.durationMs and completed_at: event.timestamp (or do one final REST load).
failure_scenario: Run a workflow, watch it finish live via WS: Duration card shows '—' permanently until manual reload although the server recorded the duration.

title: ConfigPanel form/JSON drafts not resynced after apply; mode switch reverts edits
root_cause: The reset effect depends only on [node.id, type]. After applyJson/applyForm updates node.data.config, the other mode's draft state (values/extraDraft or draft) still holds the pre-apply snapshot. Switching modes and pressing Apply writes the stale snapshot over the newer config.
suggested_fix: Resync all draft state from node.data.config whenever it changes (or key drafts by a config revision).
failure_scenario: Edit config in JSON mode (add limit:5), apply, switch to Form to tweak query, Apply — the JSON-added limit is silently deleted because form drafts were never refreshed.

title: Run/Validate proceed after a failed save, executing the stale definition
root_cause: save() catches its own errors and resolves normally (592-593); run() and validate() do `if (dirty) await save()` then unconditionally call executeWorkflow/validateWorkflow. A failed PUT is followed by execution of the old server-side graph plus a success toast.
suggested_fix: Make save() return a boolean or rethrow; abort run/validate when the pre-save fails.
failure_scenario: User edits a node config and clicks Run while the API briefly rejects the PUT: error toast flashes, then 'Execution started' appears and the workflow runs with the previous config — wrong side effects with no indication.

title: No unsaved-changes guard; Back navigation silently discards dirty graph
root_cause: The toolbar Back link (and browser back) navigate without checking dirty; no router blocker or beforeunload handler.
suggested_fix: Add useBlocker/beforeunload prompt when dirty, or autosave.
failure_scenario: User spends minutes wiring a graph, forgets Save, clicks Back — all edits vanish without warning.

title: Drag/keyboard-delete never set dirty; Save stays disabled, edits lost
root_cause: onNodesChange/onEdgesChange are wired straight to useNodesState setters (lines 459-460, 791-792) without setDirty(true). Only addNode/deleteNode/onConnect/applyConfig mark dirty; Save is disabled when !dirty. React Flow's default Backspace deletion and node drags produce unsaveable changes.
suggested_fix: Inspect changes in the handlers and setDirty(true) for position/remove/add changes (ignore select/dimensions).
failure_scenario: User repositions nodes or deletes an edge with Backspace, clicks Save — button disabled. Navigates away; layout/deletion silently lost on reload.

title: templates/*.json data directory not copied into runtime image
root_cause: TemplateRegistry.resolveDir looks for <moduleRoot>/templates (= /app/templates in image) and cwd walk-ups; the repo-root templates/ directory with marketplace JSON is never COPYed into the runtime layout.
suggested_fix: COPY templates/ ./templates/ in the runtime stage (after fixing the @loop/templates package copy).
failure_scenario: Docker deployments load 0 templates with 0 load errors — silent feature loss; POST /api/v1/templates/:id/instantiate 404s for every shipped template.

title: Helm chart points at PostgreSQL/Redis services it never creates
root_cause: values.yaml enables postgresql/redis (87-121) and deployments reference {{ .Release.Name }}-postgresql and -redis-master, but Chart.yaml declares no dependencies and templates/ contains no postgres/redis resources. LOOP_REDIS_URL also omits the password despite redis.auth.enabled=true.
suggested_fix: Add bitnami postgresql/redis as chart dependencies (or document external endpoints and make hosts configurable); include the Redis password in LOOP_REDIS_URL.
failure_scenario: helm install with default values deploys an API configured for LOOP_DB_TYPE=postgres against a nonexistent host; every pod crash-loops on DB connection. Scale-tier chart unusable as shipped.

title: desk.list_conversations silently drops the canvas status filter
root_cause: list_conversations calls callDesk with no query parameters and ignores params.input entirely, while the canvas form offers a status select (open/pending/resolved/all, WorkflowEditor.tsx:146-148).
suggested_fix: Forward input.status (and other supported filters) as URLSearchParams on the GET.
failure_scenario: Workflow configured to list only open conversations receives all including resolved ones; a downstream auto-responder replies to already-resolved tickets.

title: generic.rest_call ignores per-node headers input (config only)
root_cause: headers read only from params.config['headers']; the canvas generic.rest_call form exposes 'Headers (JSON)' landing in params.input['headers'] (WorkflowEditor.tsx:186), never consulted.
suggested_fix: Merge input.headers over config.headers (string values only) before dispatch.
failure_scenario: Node whose Authorization header is set in the UI form sends the request unauthenticated — 401, or silently different behavior on anonymous-access endpoints.

title: Unbounded response buffering in generic REST adapter
root_cause: response.body.text() buffers the entire upstream response with no size cap; target URL is arbitrary workflow input (egress-gated for destination, not size).
suggested_fix: Stream the body with a byte cap (e.g. 10 MB) and throw a clear UpstreamError when exceeded; consider configurable limit.
failure_scenario: rest_call node pointed at a large data-export/file URL buffers gigabytes into the heap; the modular-monolith API OOM-crashes, killing every in-flight execution.

title: Slack send ignores {ok:false} and HTTP status; body never drained
root_cause: SlackNotifier.send never reads response.statusCode or body. Slack returns HTTP 200 with {ok:false,error:...} for invalid tokens/channels; an unread undici body holds the socket (rest of repo explicitly drains bodies for this reason). Latent: notifiers exported but not yet wired into apps/api.
suggested_fix: Drain/parse JSON, throw on non-2xx or ok:false so NotificationQueue can retry.
failure_scenario: Misconfigured Slack token makes every notification silently 'succeed' while nothing is delivered; each send leaks a pooled socket.

title: Slack/Webhook notifiers bypass the egress policy engine (latent)
root_cause: Neither notifier accepts or calls the egress gate before dispatching to slack.com / an arbitrary webhook URL, unlike every ConnectorAdapter. Airgap mode is specified to block ALL outbound calls. Latent: not yet wired.
suggested_fix: Accept the same { check(url) } gate as ExecuteParams.egress and await it before each request; thread signal too.
failure_scenario: Once wired per TSD §9.6, notifications flow to external hosts even with LOOP_AIRGAP_MODE=true or default-deny — the sovereignty guarantee silently has a hole.

title: Webhook send ignores response status; body never drained
root_cause: WebhookNotifier.send discards the response without checking statusCode; NotificationQueue retries only thrown errors, so HTTP-level failures are never retried. Unread body holds the socket. Latent: not yet wired.
suggested_fix: Check statusCode>=400 and throw; drain the body on every path.
failure_scenario: Webhook receiver returning 500/401 treated as successful delivery; notification lost with no retry and no log.

title: Recap get_meeting id not URL-encoded — path traversal with JWT
root_cause: get_meeting interpolates String(params.input['id']) raw into the path; vault (45-49) and desk (45,57,68) use encodeURIComponent but recap does not. URL normalization resolves '..' segments before dispatch.
suggested_fix: encodeURIComponent(String(params.input['id'])) as in the sibling adapters.
failure_scenario: Meeting id from a trigger payload like '../../sync' or 'x?foo=bar' changes the request path/query (GET /meetings/../../sync -> /sync), sending the instance Bearer JWT to an unintended Recap endpoint.
verification_notes: recap get_meeting now encodeURIComponent's the id (parity with vault/desk). Regression: recap-adapter.test.ts audit #38 (id '../../sync' arrives as /meetings/..%2F..%2Fsync on a capture server). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 710/710 (56 files); integration 177/178 (pre-existing vault failure only); e2e 30/30; eslint 0 new errors.

title: Connector healthCheck bypasses egress gate and has no timeout (/ready SSRF oracle)
root_cause: healthCheck issues undici request(baseUrl+'/health') with no egress.check and no signal/timeout; same in desk/adapter.ts:75-84 and recap/adapter.ts:57-66. interface.ts:43-44 gives healthCheck no egress/signal parameters. Connector instances (editor+ role) accept arbitrary config.base_url with no URL validation (routes/index.ts:625-662). /ready (server.ts:333-350) calls healthCheckAll() on every registered instance, so the private-address blocklist and LOOP_AIRGAP_MODE are not applied on this path.
suggested_fix: Route probes through the same EgressGate (or skip probing in airgap), validate base_url at instance creation, add a short abortable timeout.
failure_scenario: LOOP_AIRGAP_MODE=true yet /ready still makes outbound GETs to configured hosts. With allowPrivate=false an editor registers base_url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data: every /ready probe issues a blind GET into the metadata/internal network, bypassing the SSRF blocklist enforced on execute().

title: Canvas rag_query sends 'question'; adapter reads 'query' -> empty RAG query
root_cause: postQuery builds the Vault body from input['query']/top_k/top_k_chunks/folder_filter, but canvas FIELD_SPECS for vault.rag_query use question/context/output_format (WorkflowEditor.tsx:133-137); vault.search offers limit/filters while the adapter reads top_k/folder_filter; create_document offers tags/folder which uploadDocument (143-148) never sends. Executor passes node.config through verbatim — no mapping layer.
suggested_fix: Accept canvas keys as aliases (question->query, limit->top_k_chunks, filters->folder_filter) or align canvas field keys; forward tags/folder in the upload form.
failure_scenario: User builds a RAG node and types a question: node POSTs /query with {query:'',top_k_chunks:8}; Vault answers an empty query and the workflow silently continues with irrelevant/empty results.

title: Egress denial rewrapped as UPSTREAM_*_UNAVAILABLE (vault/desk/recap)
root_cause: Catch-all wraps every non-UpstreamError — including the gate's LoopError('NODE_EGRESS_BLOCKED',403) thrown by egress.check — into UpstreamError('UPSTREAM_VAULT_UNAVAILABLE',502). Identical in desk/adapter.ts:135-139 and recap/adapter.ts:132-136. Generic adapter and LLM providers correctly let it propagate.
suggested_fix: Rethrow LoopError instances with code NODE_EGRESS_BLOCKED unchanged; wrap only transport errors.
failure_scenario: In airgap or under a deny policy the node fails as 502 'Vault unavailable' and the executor's default retry (LOOP_DEFAULT_RETRY_COUNT=3) retries a permanently blocked call; operators see a phantom upstream outage instead of a policy block.
verification_notes: vault/desk/recap catch blocks rethrow LoopError instances unchanged (NODE_EGRESS_BLOCKED no longer wrapped as UPSTREAM_*_UNAVAILABLE; executor will not retry policy denials as outages). Regression: tests/unit/connectors/egress-propagation.test.ts (all three adapters preserve the LoopError code, not UpstreamError). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 710/710; integration 177/178 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30.

title: Region egress policies can never match: lookupRegion is a permanent stub
root_cause: lookupRegion(_ip) returns '' unconditionally (no GeoIP source). Region allow/deny policies therefore never match in any real deployment. tests/unit/egress/engine.test.ts:18-24 mocks a fake lookupRegion (203.0.113.*->EU) and 'proves' region enforcement against the very function whose real implementation is dead — masking the gap.
suggested_fix: Implement GeoIP (e.g. MaxMind) or surface the limitation in the policy API/docs and reject region policies at creation until supported; add a test asserting the shipped resolver's actual behavior.
failure_scenario: Operator configures 'deny region RU' (data-residency requirement) alongside an allow policy: lookupRegion returns '' for every IP, the deny never matches, traffic flows to the blocked region — while the unit suite 'proves' region enforcement works.

title: LOOP_MAX_CONCURRENT caps nodes per level, not concurrent executions
root_cause: maxConcurrent only used as batch size inside one execution's executeLevel (449). Nothing limits simultaneous execute() calls: every trigger path (cron/webhook/event/manual/recovery) fire-and-forgets executor.execute immediately. TSD §13 defines LOOP_MAX_CONCURRENT as 'Max concurrent executions' (50 Core); §8.1 requires a concurrency limit check at trigger time.
suggested_fix: Add an executor-wide semaphore/queue gating execute() entry at maxConcurrent (or per-workflow/in-flight cap in dispatch paths).
failure_scenario: */1 cron on a 10-minute workflow plus webhook bursts produces hundreds of simultaneous executions, each running up to 50 nodes per level. Documented 50-execution cap and SQLite 'hard cap at 50 concurrent' assumption violated -> SQLITE_BUSY write contention, memory growth, upstream rate-limit failures.

title: Connector dispatch always uses the first instance of a type
root_cause: dispatchNode picks instanceId via listInstances().find(first matching adapterType). Registry keys insertion-ordered; env instances (vault-default/desk-default/recap-default) registered before DB instances; no per-node instance selection. Additional instances created via POST /api/v1/connectors silently never used.
suggested_fix: Support per-node instance selection (config.connector_instance_id validated against registry) or at least prefer DB-registered instances over env defaults and warn when multiple instances of a type exist.
failure_scenario: Operator sets LOOP_VAULT_URL=old-vault then creates a new vault instance pointing at migrated-vault via POST /connectors: every vault.* node still resolves vault-default (registered first) and calls the old Vault with the old API key — writes go to the decommissioned system while GET /connectors shows the new instance.

title: Inline sub-workflow definitions bypass node-type validation
root_cause: validateInlineDefinition checks only structure (ids, edges, cycles). dispatchNode (793-804) passes unknown connector types through as input=output with only a warning. The API's assertKnownNodeTypes guard (routes/index.ts:210) covers stored definitions only, so inline workflow.invoke children reintroduce the 'green no-op' bug class it was added to fix.
suggested_fix: Run the known-node-type check inside validateInlineDefinition, or make dispatchNode fail on unknown non-control connector types.
failure_scenario: workflow.invoke with inline definition containing typo'd type 'vualt.search': child node 'succeeds' echoing its input, child and parent report success, no Vault call ever happens — silent no-op execution.

title: Branch tokenizer ignores escapes; quoted strings invert decisions
root_cause: evalCondition interpolates values with JSON.stringify (escapes embedded double quotes as \"), but tokenize's string-literal scanner uses indexOf(ch, i+1) with no escape handling (comment: 'no escapes'). A serialized value containing a double quote terminates the string early at the escaped quote; remainder fails to tokenize, parse throws, evalCondition fails closed to false — even when the comparison should be true.
suggested_fix: Handle backslash escapes in the string-literal scanner, or pass values as pre-tokenized literals instead of re-parsing JSON text.
failure_scenario: Condition {{trigger.payload.name}} == {{variables.expected}} with both equal to O"Brien: both serialize to "O\"Brien", tokenizer reads string O\ then chokes -> parse error -> branch=false. Equal-values case takes the false arm; any payload string containing a double quote can never match.
verification_notes: Tokenizer string scanner now honours backslash escapes; double-quoted literals are JSON.parse'd (interpolation emits JSON.stringify) with raw-text fallback for hand-written literals. Regression: nodes.test.ts audit #46 (O"Brien equality true, differing quotes false, backslash/newline round-trip). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 700/700; integration 177/178 (pre-existing vault failure only); e2e 30/30; eslint 0 new errors.

title: Resume re-dispatches ambiguous in-flight node despite unsafe-side-effect policy
root_cause: recover() marks a 'running' execution failed when zero nodes completed ('in-flight node's side effects are ambiguous') but resumes when >=1 completed — re-dispatching the same ambiguous in-flight node (executeNodeInner resets a 'running' row and dispatches again). Idempotency-key mitigation is best-effort: GenericAdapter never forwards an Idempotency-Key header, so generic REST side effects have no dedup vector.
suggested_fix: Apply the ambiguity policy per node: on resume settle crash-interrupted 'running' node rows to failed (or require explicit confirmation) instead of silently re-dispatching; alternatively make idempotency-key forwarding mandatory for mutating connector operations.
failure_scenario: Node A succeeds; node B (generic POST /charge) in flight when process crashes after upstream applied the charge. Restart -> recovery resumes (lastCompleted=A) -> B re-dispatched -> second charge. Identical crash with zero completed nodes deliberately failed instead — policy inconsistent.

title: Malformed extra-provider entry logged with api_key intact
root_cause: logger.warn({ extra }, ...) serializes the whole parsed entry — including api_key — when name/base_url validation fails. Line 147's JSON-parse error log can also echo a snippet of the raw string.
suggested_fix: Log only the entry name and which fields are missing; never the raw object.
failure_scenario: LOOP_LLM_EXTRA_PROVIDERS='[{"name":"gw","api_key":"sk-live-..."}]' (base_url typo/omitted) writes the live vendor key into server logs on every startup.
verification_notes: factory logs only entry name + missing fields for malformed extra providers; JSON-parse failure logs the error class only (Node parse messages can echo raw snippets containing api_key). Regression: factory.test.ts audit #48 (warn/error spies never contain the key). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 710/710; integration 177/178 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30.

title: Gemini prompt-level block returns empty content as 'STOP'
root_cause: promptFeedback.blockReason never inspected; a blocked prompt yields no candidates so content='' and finish_reason defaults to 'STOP' — indistinguishable from a legitimate empty completion. Candidate-level SAFETY at least visible via finishReason.
suggested_fix: When promptFeedback.blockReason set, throw UpstreamError or map to a distinct finish_reason.
failure_scenario: Prompt hits Gemini's blocklist: API returns {promptFeedback:{blockReason:'SAFETY'}} and the workflow proceeds with an empty string as a successful answer, silently corrupting downstream steps.

title: LOOP_LLM_TIMEOUT_MS discarded when executor signal present
root_cause: signal: io?.signal ?? AbortSignal.timeout(this.timeoutMs) — the executor always passes a fused node-timeout signal (executor.ts:675-697,837), so the configured provider timeout never applies on the workflow path. Identical at anthropic.ts:45, azure.ts:36, gemini.ts:60, ollama.ts:36 and 74.
suggested_fix: Combine deadlines: AbortSignal.any([io.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(this.timeoutMs)]) (Node 20+), or race whichever fires first.
failure_scenario: Admin sets LOOP_LLM_TIMEOUT_MS=15000 to fail fast; a node with timeout_ms=600000 against a blackholed provider hangs 10 minutes instead of 15s, stalling the workflow past the intended LLM budget.
verification_notes: All providers (openai/anthropic/azure/gemini/ollama x2) now combine deadlines: AbortSignal.any([io.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(this.timeoutMs)]) when an executor signal is present — LOOP_LLM_TIMEOUT_MS applies on the workflow path again. Regression: providers.test.ts audit #50 (provider timeout fires despite a live executor signal; executor abort still cancels). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 710/710; integration 177/178 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30.

title: Non-JSON 200 provider reply crashes with raw SyntaxError
root_cause: response.body.json() on a 200 HTML page (proxy/captive portal/wrong port) throws bare SyntaxError — not UpstreamError — losing upstream context; body left undrained (socket held). Same at anthropic.ts:53, azure.ts:44, gemini.ts:68, ollama.ts:44 and 80. Generic connector already fixed this pattern (generic/adapter.ts:74-92).
suggested_fix: Read text first, attempt JSON.parse, throw UpstreamError with short snippet on failure; drain on every path.
failure_scenario: Corporate proxy returns a 200 login page for api.openai.com: node fails with "Unexpected token '<'...", circuit counts an unclassifiable failure, socket leaks.

title: Circuit breaker counts aborts/egress denials as provider failures
root_cause: Every catch increments circuit.failures with no error classification, and the loop keeps walking the chain after io.signal aborts — each remaining provider tried with the dead signal and counted as a failure. NODE_EGRESS_BLOCKED and 4xx client errors count the same as outages.
suggested_fix: Break when io?.signal?.aborted; exclude abort/cancellation, egress denials, and permanent 4xx (except 429) from failure counting.
failure_scenario: Default node timeout 30s while ollama cold starts exceed it: each timed-out LLM node increments EVERY provider's failure counter; five such nodes open all circuits and subsequent llm.complete calls fail 'No LLM providers available' for 30s. In airgap, five blocked calls likewise mask NODE_EGRESS_BLOCKED behind that generic error.
verification_notes: Router complete(): breaks the chain when io.signal aborted; NODE_EGRESS_BLOCKED denials no longer increment circuit failures (4xx classification deferred — UpstreamError carries no status field; noted as follow-up). Regression: router.test.ts audit #52 (7 denials keep circuit closed and surface the policy code; aborted signal stops the chain). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 710/710; integration 177/178 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30.

title: OTLP exporter: unbounded per-span fetches, no queue or batching
root_cause: Every span.end() fires an individual HTTP POST (single-span OTLP batch) with a 2s abort budget, no cap on in-flight requests, no queue, no batching; JSON.stringify runs synchronously in the span-end hot path. Default TRACE_SAMPLE_RATE=1.0 exports every span.
suggested_fix: Buffer spans and flush batches on interval/size with a bounded queue (drop-oldest on overflow) and concurrency limit; keep export() non-blocking.
failure_scenario: TRACE_EXPORTER=otlp with a slow/unreachable collector: 50 concurrent workflows emitting node spans accumulate hundreds of in-flight 2s POSTs; sockets/memory grow without bound, degrading the API.

title: require() in ESM makes all Prometheus metrics silent no-ops
root_cause: Package is ESM (package.json type:module, tsconfig Node16); bare require('prom-client') throws ReferenceError at runtime; tryLoadPromClient swallows it and returns undefined. metricsRegistry() always returns no-op stubs and collectMetrics() (207-211) always returns '' in the built product despite prom-client being installed.
suggested_fix: Use createRequire(import.meta.url)('prom-client') or a cached dynamic import; add a unit test asserting real counters when prom-client is installed.
failure_scenario: Production /metrics (server.ts:351) returns 200 with empty body; loop_executions_total, egress_blocked_total, circuit-breaker gauges never record. Monitoring dashboards/alerts silently blind.

title: set() without scope_id silently overwrites another scope's secret
root_cause: store.secrets.getByName omits the scope_id condition when scopeId is undefined (sqlite/index.ts:542, postgres/index.ts:619), so getByName(name, scope, undefined) matches the FIRST row with that name+scope regardless of scope_id; set() then updates that row. POST /api/v1/secrets allows scope 'connector'/'workflow' with scope_id optional (routes/index.ts:795-800).
suggested_fix: Treat undefined scope_id as NULL and match exactly (scope_id IS NULL) in getByName; require scope_id for connector/workflow scopes in the route schema.
failure_scenario: Admin POSTs /api/v1/secrets {name:'api_key',scope:'connector',value:'X'} without scope_id -> matches connector A's encrypted key row -> overwrites with X -> connector A's upstream calls fail/authenticate wrong, no conflict error. Same-scope duplicate POSTs silently upsert instead of the 409 the route comment promises.
verification_notes: getByName in both stores now matches scope_id exactly (IS NULL when undefined) instead of ignoring it; POST /api/v1/secrets requires scope_id for connector/workflow scopes (400 otherwise). Regression: manager.test.ts audit #55 (scope-less lookup never matches another scope_id row), postgres.test.ts (scope_id IS NULL SQL), admin-routes secrets API (400 without scope_id). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 691/691; integration 176/177 (pre-existing vault failure only); e2e 30/30; eslint 0 new errors.

title: PG workflows created_at/updated_at are Date objects cast as string
root_cause: node-postgres parses TIMESTAMP to Date. Inline workflow mappers in create (156), getById (163), list (184) cast created_at/updated_at 'as string' without toIsoString, unlike mapTrigger/mapConnector/users/audit mappers which call toIsoString. SQLite returns ISO strings.
suggested_fix: Wrap workflow created_at/updated_at with toIsoString(...) in all three inline mappers.
failure_scenario: String operations on workflow.updated_at (.slice, lexicographic compare, === ISO string) throw or return false on PG while working on SQLite; masked only at the HTTP boundary where JSON.stringify coerces Date.
verification_notes: PG workflows create/getById/list mappers wrap created_at/updated_at with toIsoString (parity with other PG mappers and SQLite). Regression: postgres.test.ts audit #56 (Date row -> ISO string). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 691/691; integration 176/177 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30.

title: Workflow search/tag filter semantics diverge between SQLite and PG
root_cause: SQLite workflows.list (sqlite/index.ts:133-139) uses substring LIKE for tag (on JSON text) and search (name/description). PG uses tags @> '[tag]' (exact element) and to_tsvector @@ plainto_tsquery (lexeme/stem full-text). Different matching semantics for the same WorkflowFilter contract.
suggested_fix: Pick one semantics for both tiers (exact tag membership + defined search behavior) and implement identically; document search behavior.
failure_scenario: Search 'work' matches 'workflow' on Core (LIKE %work%) but nothing on Scale (FTS lexeme). Tag 'prod' matches 'production' on Core but not Scale. Same API query, different result sets per tier.
verification_notes: Aligned both tiers to substring semantics: PG search now LIKE on name/description (was FTS lexeme), PG tag now tags::text LIKE (was exact @>), matching SQLite's existing substring behavior; LIKE metacharacters escaped. Exact-element tag matching on both tiers is blocked by #60 (double-encoded SQLite JSON) — noted in code. Regression: egress-and-filter.test.ts (tag+search substring on SQLite). PG SQL verified statically (no local PG). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 691/691; integration 176/177 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30.

title: PG secrets.encrypted_value is BYTEA; getByName returns Buffer, not string
root_cause: migrations-pg.ts:125 defines encrypted_value BYTEA while interface/SQLite use TEXT/string. create/update bind the JSON ciphertext string into BYTEA (bytea escape-format input); getByName casts r.encrypted_value 'as string' (line 623) but node-postgres returns BYTEA as Buffer. Contract violated; diverges from SQLite.
suggested_fix: Store encrypted_value as TEXT in PG (matches SQLite/interface), or bind Buffer.from(value,'utf8') on write and return .toString('utf8') on read.
failure_scenario: SecretsManager.get survives only because JSON.parse(Buffer) coerces via toString. Any direct string use gets a Buffer; bytea escape-format input parsing corrupts payloads containing backslashes. SQLite returns a real string for the same call.
verification_notes: PG secrets create/update bind Buffer.from(value,'utf8') (bytea hex format — avoids escape-format backslash corruption); getByName converts Buffer back to string, honouring the interface contract. Regression: postgres.test.ts audit #58 (Buffer param on write; string on read). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 691/691; integration 176/177 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30. Column stays BYTEA (no migration needed).

title: PG migration runner is check-then-act with no advisory lock
root_cause: runPostgresMigrations reads applied versions then applies pending migrations in per-migration transactions; nothing serializes concurrent runners. CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS still races under concurrent DDL; INSERT INTO schema_migrations collides on the version PK.
suggested_fix: Take pg_advisory_lock around the whole migration run; re-read applied versions inside the lock.
failure_scenario: Two Scale replicas boot against a fresh DB: both see migration 001 unapplied, both BEGIN+CREATE+INSERT. Second hits PK/concurrent-CREATE error, rolls back and throws -> replica fails to start during rolling deploy.

title: SQLite json-mode columns double-encode JSON (callers pre-stringify)
root_cause: schema.ts declares definition/tags/trigger_payload/input/output/metadata/payload/config/details as text(...,{mode:'json'}); drizzle 0.29.5 SQLiteTextJson.mapToDriverValue already JSON.stringify's. The store passes an ALREADY-stringified string (JSON.stringify(data.definition) as never), so the DB stores a JSON-string-of-JSON. Reads round-trip only because mapFromDriverValue parses once and safeJsonParse re-parses. Systemic across every json column in this file.
suggested_fix: Pass raw objects to drizzle json-mode columns (let drizzle serialize once), or switch columns to plain text mode and keep manual stringify. Never both.
failure_scenario: SELECT json_extract(definition,'$.nodes') FROM workflows returns NULL on SQLite (top-level value is a JSON string, not object); the equivalent PG JSONB column works. Core->Scale data migration or any external SQL/analytics consumer sees corrupted double-encoded data masked in-app by safeJsonParse.

title: SQLite egressPolicies.update throws 'No values to set' on empty patch
root_cause: update passes all six optional fields straight into drizzle .set(); an empty patch leaves every value undefined and drizzle 0.29.5 mapUpdateSet throws Error('No values to set'). PG adapter (postgres/index.ts:688) returns early when setClauses is empty.
suggested_fix: Mirror PG: build the set conditionally and return early when no field is provided.
failure_scenario: PUT /api/v1/egress/policies/:id with body {} passes the all-optional schema and reaches store.egressPolicies.update(id,{}): Core (SQLite) throws -> 500; Scale (PG) no-ops -> 200.
verification_notes: SQLite egressPolicies.update builds the set conditionally and returns early on an empty patch (PG parity) — drizzle no longer throws 'No values to set'. Regression: egress-and-filter.test.ts audit #61 (empty patch resolves; partial patch applies). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 691/691; integration 176/177 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30.

title: register() unregisters existing job before validating; PUT rollback never restores schedule
root_cause: register() calls this.unregister(triggerId) first, then cron.validate; when validation throws the previously working schedule is already stopped. PUT /api/v1/triggers/:triggerId (routes/index.ts:501-517) unregisters, relies on register throwing to roll back the DB config, but never re-registers the old schedule — DB and scheduler diverge.
suggested_fix: Validate the new expression (and construct the task) before unregistering the existing job; only swap once the replacement is created. Alternatively re-register the old config in the route's catch after rollback.
failure_scenario: PUT /api/v1/triggers/<enabled cron> {config:{expression:'not-a-cron'}} -> 400 returned, DB unchanged (enabled, valid expression), but the cron job was unregistered and never restored -> schedule silently stops firing until server restart.
verification_notes: cron.register validates the expression BEFORE unregistering the existing job; PUT /triggers no longer pre-unregisters (register swaps atomically; unregister only on disable), so a rejected expression leaves the old schedule running and the DB rollback stays consistent. Regression: cron.test.ts (rejected re-registration keeps firing) + admin-routes.test.ts (PUT invalid -> 400, DB rolled back, old every-second schedule still creates executions). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 700/700; integration 177/178 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30.

title: Cron tick failures silently swallowed (no task-failed listener)
root_cause: executions.create sits outside any try/catch in the async tick callback. node-cron@3.0.3 Task.execute catches the rejected promise and emits 'task-failed', but CronTriggerHandler attaches no listener, so a tick failing before/while creating the execution vanishes with zero logs and no failed execution record.
suggested_fix: Wrap the whole tick body in try/catch that logs and records a failed execution when possible; attach task.on('task-failed', ...) logger in register().
failure_scenario: SQLite momentarily locked/IO-errors at fire time: executions.create throws, async callback rejects, node-cron emits 'task-failed' to nobody. Scheduled run lost with no log line, no execution row, no alert — operators see a cron trigger that 'didn't fire'.
verification_notes: Cron tick wraps executions.create in try/catch with an error log; register() attaches a task-failed listener so node-cron's swallowed rejections are logged. Regression: cron.test.ts (create rejects -> tick handled, no unhandled rejection). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 700/700; integration 177/178 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30.

title: Event triggers fire for archived workflows (no fire-time guard)
root_cause: TriggerDispatcher.dispatch matches enabled event triggers and creates executions without checking workflow.status. Cron (cron.ts:69) and webhook (webhook.ts:66) have fire-time archived guards because registered triggers outlive archiving; the event path lacks it. Archiving via PUT /workflows/:id {status:'archived'} does not disarm triggers (only DELETE does, best-effort). The version read at 50-51 already fetches the row.
suggested_fix: Load the workflow in dispatch() and skip (or disable the trigger) when status==='archived', mirroring cron/webhook.
failure_scenario: Workflow with event trigger archived via PUT (triggers stay enabled): POST /api/v1/events with matching source/event_type creates an execution and runExecution executes the archived definition — real side effects for a 'deleted' flow.
verification_notes: TriggerDispatcher.dispatch skips archived workflows at fire time (mirrors cron/webhook guards), logging the skip. Regression: dispatcher.test.ts audit #64 (archived workflow -> no execution). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 685/685; integration 174/175 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30; eslint delta 0 (new mock typed without any).

title: Spec-mandated webhook timestamp replay protection is missing
root_cause: File header claims 'HMAC-SHA256 signature verification + replay protection (§11.6)' but TSD §11.6 requires 'timestamp in signature payload; reject if > 5 minutes old'. handle() verifies only HMAC over the raw body; no timestamp/nonce check. The 60/min rate limit is not replay protection.
suggested_fix: Require a signed timestamp (header included in HMAC input or signed payload field), reject requests older than 5 minutes, optionally track recent signature nonces per trigger.
failure_scenario: Attacker capturing one valid signed webhook request (log, proxy, browser history) replays it indefinitely at up to 60/min; each replay passes HMAC and creates a new execution, re-firing side effects with no expiry.

title: Trigger config catch-all union voids webhook secret requirement
root_cause: TriggerConfigSchema unions typed configs with z.record(z.unknown()) so any object validates; WebhookTriggerConfigSchema.secret has no min length. The create route (routes/index.ts:429+) enforces cron/event branches but not webhook, and WebhookTriggerHandler accepts unsigned events when config.secret is falsy (triggers/webhook.ts:37).
suggested_fix: Discriminate the union on trigger_type (or validate per-type in the route), require secret.min(16) for webhook triggers, auto-generate a secret at creation.
failure_scenario: POST /api/v1/workflows/:id/triggers {trigger_type:'webhook',config:{}} creates a secret-less trigger; anyone learning the trigger UUID can fire executions with arbitrary payloads via POST /webhooks/:triggerId without signature — unauthenticated side effects.
verification_notes: Create route enforces webhook branch: config.secret must be a string >= 16 chars (400 VALIDATION_REQUIRED otherwise), matching the cron/event enforcement pattern; WebhookTriggerConfigSchema.secret now .min(16). Existing fixtures with short secrets updated to the new contract. Regression: trigger-to-execution.test.ts audit #66 (missing + short secret -> 400). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 685/685; integration 174/175 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30; eslint delta 0. Note: auto-generation of secrets at creation not implemented (require-only, minimal scope); unsigned-legacy-trigger acceptance in webhook.ts remains for pre-existing rows.

title: Unbounded node timeout_ms overflows setTimeout, instant NODE_TIMEOUT
root_cause: WorkflowNodeSchema.timeout_ms is z.number().int().positive() with no max; executor uses it unclamped in withTimeout's setTimeout (executor.ts:490,684). Delays > 2^31-1 fire after 1ms.
suggested_fix: Add .max(2_147_483_647) or clamp in withTimeout.
failure_scenario: Long-running node sets timeout_ms=3000000000 (~35 days): node rejected with NODE_TIMEOUT after ~1ms on every attempt, retries exhaust, execution fails despite a 'generous' timeout.
verification_notes: WorkflowNodeSchema.timeout_ms now .max(2_147_483_647); executor clamps node timeout at the use site (covers legacy stored definitions). Regression: timeout-bounds.test.ts (max accepted, 3e9 rejected). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 700/700; integration 177/178 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30.

title: Unbounded workflow_timeout_ms overflows setTimeout, aborts in 1ms
root_cause: WorkflowSettingsSchema.workflow_timeout_ms is z.number().int().positive() with no max. Executor passes it straight to setTimeout (executor.ts:290-293); Node clamps delays > 2^31-1 to 1ms (TimeoutOverflowWarning).
suggested_fix: Cap at 2_147_483_647 (or a product max like 7 days) in the schema and/or clamp in the executor.
failure_scenario: Approval workflow sets workflow_timeout_ms=2592000000 (30 days): every execution aborts after ~1ms with WORKFLOW_TIMEOUT; workflow can never succeed and the error misreports the configured timeout.
verification_notes: WorkflowSettingsSchema.workflow_timeout_ms now .max(2_147_483_647); executor clamps the workflow deadline at the use site. Regression: timeout-bounds.test.ts (max accepted, 30-day value rejected). Verified: typecheck 0; unit 700/700; integration 177/178 (pre-existing only); e2e 30/30.

title: Git commit sequence unserialized; concurrent versions race on index/HEAD
root_cause: commit() does writeFileSync -> git.add -> git.commit against the shared .git/index and HEAD with no mutex; isomorphic-git provides no cross-call locking. VersioningService.createVersion is invoked from authoring.update/restoreVersion which can run concurrently.
suggested_fix: Serialize all GitBackend mutations per repo (async mutex around write+add+commit, or single-writer queue).
failure_scenario: Two concurrent createVersion calls stage into the shared index and commit: a commit can snapshot wrong index contents, or both read the same parent HEAD and the second ref write orphans the first commit -> lost/corrupted version history.

title: createVersion commits to git before DB insert with no compensation
root_cause: git.commit runs first (line 30), then store.workflowDefinitions.create (line 40). Two-phase write spans git + DB with no transaction/compensation; if the DB insert fails the git commit is already persisted.
suggested_fix: Insert the DB snapshot first, or add a compensating action on failure; treat git as rebuildable from the snapshot table.
failure_scenario: git.commit succeeds, workflowDefinitions.create throws (UNIQUE conflict from concurrent update, DB outage). Caller sees error but git history advanced with an unreferenced commit; retries add more. Git history permanently diverges from the authoritative snapshot table.

title: Sandbox isolation asserted against a test-local mock, not the system
root_cause: startMockSandbox is a regex-based fake defined inside the test; tests 1-3 assert the fake blocks fs/network. 'Integrates with executor' tests register a test-local 'code' adapter proxying to the fake. Production registers no 'code' adapter (server.ts:119-146) so code.* nodes are rejected at creation; apps/sandbox/src/server.ts returns status:'stub' with empty output. Nothing in the real dispatch chain is exercised.
suggested_fix: Mark the suite as a contract sketch until the real sandbox lands; then drive code nodes through the real adapter + apps/sandbox and assert blocked status fails the execution. At minimum assert the stub's status:'stub' is treated as failure, not success.
failure_scenario: A future real code adapter ignoring the sandbox 'blocked' status (or treating stub output as success) ships green: the suite only proves its own mock returns 'blocked' for code containing 'fs'.

title: Egress 'E2E' never exercises the connector call path it claims to wire
root_cause: Header claims the interceptor is wired into a workflow's connector call path but no workflow is executed anywhere in the file; all tests call egressEngine.evaluate / EgressInterceptor.request directly, duplicating integration/security/egress.test.ts. The allow-policy test explicitly abandons the real call (comment 153-156). Mock adapters in helpers.ts never do HTTP.
suggested_fix: Replace decision-only tests with real execution: executor wired with gate + real adapter pointed at loopback mock server; assert blocked domain fails NODE_EGRESS_BLOCKED and allowed domain reaches the mock exactly once.
failure_scenario: The interceptor-to-adapter contract (adapter must consult params.egress before every call) is untested end-to-end; an adapter skipping the check passes this entire 'E2E egress enforcement' suite.

title: 'Startup runs recovery automatically' test never starts an app
root_cause: The test just calls new ExecutionRecovery(ctx.store).recover() directly — identical to the four preceding tests; comment (312-314) admits buildApp is not invoked. helpers.ts:135 builds ExecutionRecovery without the re-dispatch callback; crash-recovery.test.ts re-executes manually. The production startup chain (server.ts:269-294: recover -> dispatchToExecutor -> executor.execute) is never exercised end-to-end.
suggested_fix: Use a file-backed SQLite DB, seed an interrupted execution, call real buildApp() on the same DB path, assert the execution is re-dispatched to terminal state without manual executor invocation.
failure_scenario: A regression where recovery resets executions to 'pending' but nothing re-dispatches them (original bugs 12/13) ships green: every recovery test drives the executor by hand.

title: RBAC E2E asserts a test-local permission table, enforces nothing
root_cause: isAllowed (18-25) is a permission map defined in the test using legacy read/write/admin roles, divergent from production requireRole's admin/editor/viewer model. Tests assert only this local table; no HTTP request is made. Meanwhile the admin gates on POST/GET/DELETE /api/v1/secrets and /api/v1/egress/policies (routes/index.ts:686-720,802-833) have zero test coverage repo-wide (no test file contains 'api/v1/secrets').
suggested_fix: Delete the local table; drive real HTTP requests with viewer/editor JWTs against /api/v1/secrets, /api/v1/egress/policies, /api/v1/audit asserting 403 FORBIDDEN_INSUFFICIENT_ROLE.
failure_scenario: Removing preHandler:[requireRole('admin')] from the secrets routes lets any editor create/read secret metadata ship green — the 'RBAC enforcement (E2E)' suite still passes checking its own map.

title: Cron handler lacks dispatcher and shutdown; leaked node-cron timers
root_cause: buildTestApp creates CronTriggerHandler(store) with no dispatcher (production server.ts:251-253 passes dispatchToExecutor — the bug-14 fix) and registers no onClose hook calling cronHandler.shutdown() (production server.ts:358-368). trigger-to-execution.test.ts:191-213 registers a '*/5 * * * *' cron trigger never unregistered; node-cron@3.0.3 timers are not unref'd; afterAll closes app/conn but the task survives.
suggested_fix: Pass a dispatcher mirroring server.ts and add app.addHook('onClose', () => cronHandler.shutdown()); add an integration test that a cron tick runs the workflow to terminal state.
failure_scenario: (1) Cron-fired executions staying 'pending' forever (production bug 14) cannot be caught by any integration test; (2) the leaked */5 task fires after conn.close() in a reused vitest worker, throwing 'database connection is not open' — unhandled rejection flaking sibling files.

title: Auth integration tests assert jose/bcrypt primitives and inline tautologies
root_cause: The 'login returns access and refresh tokens' test (36-72) never calls POST /api/v1/auth/login — it hand-signs/verifies a JWT with jose and issues no refresh token. RBAC tests (118-153) assert a locally computed boolean; deactivated-user test asserts canLogin = user.is_active. Header comment about unwired routes is stale (routes/auth.ts + createAuthGuard exist). buildTestApp never registers registerAuthRoutes: zero HTTP login coverage in the integration suite.
suggested_fix: Register auth routes in buildTestApp and rewrite as HTTP tests (login, wrong password, deactivated user, lockout); delete tautological role checks (real guard coverage lives in api/rbac.test.ts).
failure_scenario: A regression in the login route's is_active check, role mapping, or token TTL passes this 'Authentication & RBAC' integration suite because it only tests the jose library and boolean algebra.

title: Provider-failure test depends on nothing listening on localhost:11434
root_cause: Test assumes the default Ollama URL is unreachable and accepts any of 500/502/503. On developer machines running Ollama (the project's default local LLM) the call succeeds with 200 and the test fails; another service on 11434 can produce arbitrary statuses.
suggested_fix: Override LOOP_LLM_OLLAMA_URL to a guaranteed-closed port (http://127.0.0.1:1) or a mock server returning 500; assert the specific error envelope/code.
failure_scenario: Local verification flakes red for any developer running Ollama; the broad [500,502,503] acceptance hides which error path fired.

title: No unit test for expired/tampered JWT rejection or static API-key auth
root_cause: Auth unit tests cover issuance happy path, scrypt helpers, lockout, pure RBAC helpers. createAuthGuard's negative JWT paths (expired token — issuance sets 12h exp at routes/auth.ts:118; tampered signature; wrong secret) and the static LOOP_API_KEY / x-api-key path (middleware/auth.ts:170) have no unit test.
suggested_fix: Add guard tests: SignJWT with past exp -> 401; different-secret signature -> 401; valid x-api-key -> principal 'system' with LOOP_API_KEY_ROLE; wrong key -> 401.
failure_scenario: Refactor adds generous clockTolerance or drops exp verification (stolen tokens valid forever), or breaks constant-time API-key compare: issuance tests stay green.

title: Issued-token check uses .not.toBe(401); 403/500 also pass
root_cause: Guarded request hits an unregistered route, so the meaningful outcome is 404. .not.toBe(401) passes on 403 (RBAC misclassification of a valid admin token) or 500 (guard crash on a valid token), not just success.
suggested_fix: Assert expect(guarded.statusCode).toBe(404) (guard passed, route absent), or register a real protected route and assert 200 plus resolved authRole.
failure_scenario: roleFromClaims/requiredRoleFor regression rejects valid admin JWTs with 403, or guard throws 500 on well-formed tokens: login still 'issues a working token' per this test.

title: node:dns mock returns wrong shape for {all:true}; private check no-ops
root_cause: Mock lookup calls cb(null, '93.184.216.34') regardless of options. interceptor.ts calls promisified lookup with {all:true}, which really returns an ARRAY of {address,family}. With the mock it resolves to a string; firstPrivateAddress for-of's the string's characters, isPrivateIp(undefined) throws inside try, catch returns null. The hostname private-address branch is silently disabled in this whole file.
suggested_fix: Make mock honor opts.all: cb(null,[{address:'93.184.216.34',family:4}]) when all:true. Add a gate test where a hostname resolves to a private address and assert check() rejects even with an allow policy.
failure_scenario: A regression in firstPrivateAddress's DNS path makes hostname-based SSRF blocking fail open; gate.test.ts stays green because its mock already forces that path to null.

title: isAvailable .resolves assertions are never awaited
root_cause: Three expect(provider.isAvailable()).resolves.toBe(...) calls neither awaited nor returned. Test completes synchronously and reports passed; a failing assertion becomes a floating promise rejection with unreliable attribution.
suggested_fix: await each expect(...).resolves chain (or Promise.all).
failure_scenario: Regression makes isAvailable() return true for a keyless remote vendor (or false for a local server): test green; router/factory then skips or misroutes providers.

title: Archived-cron test passes vacuously if the scheduler never fires
root_cause: Test registers an every-second job, sleeps 2.2s real time, asserts created == []. No positive control that a tick happened (store.workflows.getById is a vi.fn but never asserted).
