If node-cron never fires — scheduler regression, timezone bug, blocked event loop under CI load — the assertion passes for the wrong reason.
suggested_fix: Assert expect(store.workflows.getById).toHaveBeenCalled() before asserting created == []; better, drive node-cron with vi.useFakeTimers + advanceTimersByTimeAsync.
failure_scenario: A node-cron upgrade or register() regression stops jobs firing at all: this 'archived workflows no longer trigger' test stays green while the same regression silently disables ALL cron triggers in production.

title: Path-traversal test swallows rejection and asserts on stale request log
root_cause: .catch(() => undefined) discards any execute() failure, then asserts on seen[seen.length-1]. If the adapter throws BEFORE dispatching (or no-ops), no new request is recorded and last is the previous test's '/error' request — containing neither '../' nor '/etc/passwd', so both assertions pass without any traversal request being made.
suggested_fix: Capture seen.length before the call; assert a new request was recorded (or the specific rejection code if fail-closed is intended) and that its URL contains the percent-encoded form (%2e%2e%2f).
failure_scenario: GenericAdapter regression drops the request entirely on '..' paths (or crashes pre-dispatch): test still passes, giving false confidence that traversal is 'encoded and sent'.

title: Migration idempotency test asserts >0 rows, not unchanged count
root_cause: Comment says 'Should still have same number of migrations' but assertion is only migrations.length > 0 after the second run. A runner bug re-inserting schema_migrations rows (or re-applying migrations) every startup passes. Checksum-mismatch handling also untested.
suggested_fix: Capture row count/version set after run 1, assert deep-equality after run 2; add a test that tampering with an applied migration's checksum fails loudly.
failure_scenario: migrate.ts regression loses the version check and re-applies/re-records migrations each boot: duplicate rows accumulate, future version gating misbehaves, 'idempotent' test green.

title: Mock pg client lacks rowCount: PG completeIfActive race guard untested
root_cause: createMockConn's query returns only { rows } — no rowCount — and the file never calls executions.completeIfActive. PG implementation (postgres/index.ts:348-363) decides the cancel-vs-completion race via (result.rowCount ?? 0) > 0 plus AND status IN ('pending','running'). SQLite equivalent well tested (complete-if-active.test.ts); Scale-tier copy pinned by nothing.
suggested_fix: Extend mock to return programmable rowCount; add PG tests mirroring complete-if-active.test.ts (terminal -> rowCount 0 -> false; active -> rowCount 1 -> true; assert SQL contains status guard).
failure_scenario: PG refactor drops AND status IN (...) or mis-maps rowCount: on Scale a late executor completion overwrites a user cancel (or vice versa) — the exact race M3 fixed for SQLite — and all unit tests pass.

title: 'skips disabled triggers' test exercises nothing; version snapshot unpinned
root_cause: Mock listEnabled returns [] — identical to 'no triggers exist'. Disabled-trigger filtering lives in store.triggers.listEnabled (SQL), which the mock bypasses. Mock has no workflows entity, so dispatch()'s version-snapshot call throws into catch and always defaults to 1; objectContaining assertion omits workflow_version, leaving the M5 stale-version fix unpinned.
suggested_fix: Test enablement against real SQLite store (enabled+disabled triggers, assert only enabled fires). Add workflows.getById returning version 3; assert executions.create receives workflow_version: 3.
failure_scenario: Store regression makes listEnabled return disabled rows (or dispatch regresses to hardcoded version 1, resolving stale definitions during replay): both pass this suite.

title: HMAC tests use rawBody === JSON.stringify(body); raw-byte pin is vacuous
root_cause: Every test sets rawBody = JSON.stringify(body), so a handler regression verifying HMAC over JSON.stringify(params.body) instead of params.rawBody produces identical signatures and passes — precisely the bug class the 'raw-body HMAC' commit fixed (senders with different key order/whitespace would all be rejected).
suggested_fix: Sign a rawBody differing from JSON.stringify(body) (spaces/reversed key order), pass parsed object as body, assert acceptance. Add negative case where signature matches JSON.stringify(body) but NOT rawBody, assert rejection.
failure_scenario: Someone 'simplifies' webhook.ts to re-serialize the parsed body for HMAC: all unit tests pass; in production every webhook from a sender whose serialization differs from V8's JSON.stringify gets 401.

title: Duplicate settings key silently overrides import resolver config
root_cause: Object literal defines settings twice (14-18 and 41-45); second wins, switching import/resolver from node to typescript — but eslint-import-resolver-typescript is not in devDependencies, so resolver-dependent import rules would fail to load.
suggested_fix: Merge into one settings block; add eslint-import-resolver-typescript or keep the node resolver.
failure_scenario: Enabling import/no-unresolved errors with 'unable to load resolver typescript' for every file; the dead first settings block misleads readers about the active config.

title: runWithCorrelation with empty callback is a no-op
root_cause: runWithCorrelation({request_id}, () => {}) runs an empty function, establishing no context for downstream handlers; comment claims it covers them. Correlation works only because traceIdHook (registered after) wraps Fastify's done in storage.run. Reordering/removing traceIdHook would silently lose request_id correlation.
suggested_fix: Remove the no-op call and misleading comment, or wrap the hook continuation like traceIdHook; keep a single hook responsible for ALS context.
failure_scenario: Future refactor registers traceIdHook before requestIdHook or drops it -> getCorrelationContext() undefined in handlers -> error responses and logs lose request_id with no test-visible signal.

title: scryptSync blocks the event loop in the login path
root_cause: hashPassword/verifyPassword use scryptSync (default N=16384,r=8,p=1, tens of ms) inside the request handler, stalling all concurrent requests on the single-threaded loop per login attempt.
suggested_fix: Use async crypto.scrypt (promisified) in verifyPassword/hashPassword.
failure_scenario: Burst of concurrent logins (or brute-force stream within rate limit): each attempt blocks the loop ~50-100ms; unrelated API requests and webhook deliveries queue behind KDF work.

title: Unbounded per-username lockout map grows on failed logins
root_cause: Module-level failures Map only deletes entries on successful login (clearFailures). registerFailure creates entries for nonexistent usernames too; nothing expires them; global rate limit (1000/min/IP) is the only brake.
suggested_fix: Prune expired below-threshold entries on a timer or when the map exceeds a size cap; key by username+IP or cap total entries.
failure_scenario: Attacker sprays login with random usernames at the allowed rate -> ~1.4M map entries/day accumulate permanently -> slow memory exhaustion of the API process.

title: JWT TTL config ignored; 12h expiry hard-coded
root_cause: Login signs with setExpirationTime(now + 12*60*60) and reports expires_in 12h, while config.ts:145-146 defines LOOP_JWT_ACCESS_TTL (default '15m') and LOOP_JWT_REFRESH_TTL ('7d'); neither read anywhere, no refresh endpoint exists.
suggested_fix: Parse LOOP_JWT_ACCESS_TTL and use for setExpirationTime/expires_in; implement refresh issuance or remove dead refresh config.
failure_scenario: Operator sets LOOP_JWT_ACCESS_TTL=5m expecting short-lived tokens -> issued tokens remain valid 12 hours, widening the stolen-token window 144x beyond configured policy.

title: Manual execute runs archived workflows (explicit action, no status guard)
root_cause: authoring.getById returns archived rows (workflow-authoring/service.ts:59-63, no status check) and POST /execute dispatches the definition without checking status. Cron/webhook explicitly refuse archived workflows; manual does not. Downgraded to Low because manual execution is an explicit user action (arguably intentional, like executing inactive workflows in other orchestrators) — but it defeats DELETE's stated purpose of disarming the flow, and the event-trigger path (separate Medium finding) has no such excuse.
suggested_fix: Decide and document the policy: either reject status==='archived' on POST /execute with 409 (mirroring cron/webhook), or document that manual execution of archived workflows is allowed.
failure_scenario: User DELETEs a workflow (archives, disarms triggers) -> anyone later POSTs /api/v1/workflows/<id>/execute -> archived definition runs with real connector side effects.

title: Egress policy PUT/DELETE report success for nonexistent ids
root_cause: Unlike connectors/triggers routes, PUT and DELETE /api/v1/egress/policies/:id never check existence; store update/delete affects zero rows and the route returns updated:true / deleted:true (and invalidates cache).
suggested_fix: Load the policy first and throw NotFoundError when absent, matching other resource routes.
failure_scenario: Admin UI deletes an already-deleted policy id (double click/stale list) -> API answers deleted:true -> UI believes the policy existed and was removed, masking state drift; PUT typo'd id answers updated:true while nothing changed.

title: Cron keeps firing during executor drain on shutdown
root_cause: onClose drains the executor (up to 10s) BEFORE cronHandler.shutdown(); a cron job firing inside that window creates and dispatches a new execution that store.close() then severs (completion writes fail and are swallowed).
suggested_fix: Call cronHandler.shutdown() before executor.drain() so no new executions start during the drain window.
failure_scenario: SIGTERM just before a cron tick: drain waits on old runs, cron fires mid-drain, new execution starts, store.close() runs -> execution left running/pending in DB, recovered (or failed) only on next startup.

title: Dead parallel canvas components diverge from the live editor and hide bugs
root_cause: CanvasEditor, NodeConfigPanel, NodeLibrary, CustomEdge, ExecutionMonitor and the apiClient REST object are exported but never imported by any page. They contain latent bugs (handleNodesChange passes pre-change stale nodes; NodeConfigPanel writes 'label' into config while reading node.data.label) and duplicate palette/config logic WorkflowEditor re-implemented.
suggested_fix: Delete unused modules or wire them into the editor; single source of truth for palette, config panel and API client.
failure_scenario: Developer fixes node-config UX in NodeConfigPanel.tsx (obvious name) and ships a change with zero effect because WorkflowEditor uses its own internal ConfigPanel.

title: res.json() unguarded: non-JSON error bodies surface as SyntaxError
root_cause: requestEnvelope awaits res.json() without a catch. When the API is down and the Vite proxy/gateway returns HTML/text 502, the thrown SyntaxError replaces the intended ApiError with HTTP status.
suggested_fix: Parse defensively (res.json().catch(() => null)) and throw ApiError with status when body is not a JSON envelope, as api/client.ts does.
failure_scenario: API crashes; Dashboard shows 'SyntaxError: Unexpected token <' instead of 'API unreachable (502)'.

title: No-preference theme default disagrees with pre-mount script (dark vs light)
root_cause: readInitial returns 'dark' unless prefers-color-scheme: light matches; index.html's pre-paint script (line 22) defaults to 'light' unless prefers-color-scheme: dark matches. With no OS preference both queries are false: page paints light then flips to dark at module load.
suggested_fix: Use the same query and fallback in both places (OS dark -> dark, else light).
failure_scenario: User with no OS color-scheme preference: light flash then dark UI; documented suite-wide light default not honored.

title: No React error boundary anywhere; one render exception white-screens app
root_cause: Tree rendered without any ErrorBoundary. Any render-time throw (malformed server payload reaching .map/.toLowerCase on a non-string) unmounts the entire SPA to a blank page.
suggested_fix: Wrap routes in an error boundary with reload/back fallback.
failure_scenario: Workflow row arrives with tags:null from an API variant; Workflows' w.tags.some throws during render and the whole app blanks out.

title: Dashboard stats computed from first 100 rows only; totals ignored
root_cause: listWorkflows/listExecutions fetched with per_page:100; stats (counts, success rate, 24h volume) computed over that page; meta.total discarded.
suggested_fix: Use meta.total for counts and server-side aggregates (or paged fetch) for rates/timeline.
failure_scenario: Installation with 350 workflows / 2,000 executions shows 'Workflows 100', 'Executions 100' and success rate from only the 100 most recent runs.

title: Node-usage chart tooltip mislabels counts as 'executions'
root_cause: ChartTooltip hardcodes '{value} executions' and is reused for the 'Node usage by agent' BarChart (line 305) where values are node counts.
suggested_fix: Pass a unit label prop or use a separate tooltip for the node chart.
failure_scenario: Hover 'vault' bar in 'Node usage by agent': shows '12 executions' instead of 12 nodes — misleading operational data.

title: load() lacks stale-response guard when route id changes
root_cause: api.getExecution(id).then(setExecution) has no alive/request-id check. Back/forward navigation between execution URLs re-runs load with a new id while the old fetch may be in flight; the late old response overwrites the new execution.
suggested_fix: Track an effect-scoped alive flag or compare id before applying the response.
failure_scenario: View execution A (slow request), Back then open B quickly: A's response lands last, page shows A's data under B's URL while B's live events mutate it.

title: Node trace keys differ between WS-created and REST rows; expansion collapses
root_cause: NodeTraceRow keyed by node.id: WS/snapshot rows use node_id as id (blankNode), REST rows use DB uuid. When the 4s poll replaces a WS row with its REST counterpart the key changes, remounting the row and resetting local expanded state.
suggested_fix: Key rows by node_id (stable across both sources).
failure_scenario: During a live run user expands a node's output; next poll swaps row id from 'node_3' to uuid and the panel collapses every few seconds.

title: Executions list polls every 8s unconditionally, even when idle
root_cause: Comment says 'Live refresh while any execution is running' but the interval is created regardless of active rows and never pauses on hidden tabs.
suggested_fix: Only poll when some row is active (and/or use document.visibilityState).
failure_scenario: Executions tab left open overnight on idle system: ~10,800 needless list requests, each scanning the executions table.

title: Create wizard shows Tags field for templates but silently discards it
root_cause: Template branch calls instantiateTemplate with only name/description (API accepts only those), yet step 2 renders an editable Tags input prefilled from the template. User tag edits dropped without notice.
suggested_fix: Hide/disable tags input in template mode, or apply tags via follow-up updateWorkflow.
failure_scenario: Pick template, edit tags to 'finance, prod', create — workflow carries template's original tags; user edits vanished.

title: Snapshot merge never updates status of already-known nodes
root_cause: reduceNodes's snapshot branch only inserts nodes whose node_id is unseen; existing rows keep stale status/output. Snapshot rows also lack started_at/completed_at so duration renders '—'.
suggested_fix: Merge snapshot fields (status/output/error) into existing rows, preferring newer snapshot data.
failure_scenario: REST load returns node X 'running'; X completes before WS snapshot. Snapshot says 'succeeded' but existing row kept; execution flips to succeeded (poll stops) leaving node X displayed 'running' on a finished execution.

title: Archive removes row locally; 'archived' filter shows nothing until reload
root_cause: deleteWorkflow filters the workflow out of the store instead of updating status to 'archived'. List endpoint includes archived rows; server and client disagree until next load.
suggested_fix: Update the row's status to 'archived' in place rather than removing it.
failure_scenario: Archive a workflow, click 'archived' filter — list empty though workflow exists server-side; reappears only after navigating away and back.

title: Dev server binds 0.0.0.0 and proxies /api and /metrics to loopback API
root_cause: host:'0.0.0.0' exposes the Vite dev server to the whole LAN while proxying to an API possibly bound to localhost only, bypassing the API's network isolation; /metrics also exposed without auth.
suggested_fix: Bind to localhost by default (opt-in host flag); drop /metrics proxy unless needed.
failure_scenario: pnpm dev on shared Wi-Fi with API on 127.0.0.1: anyone on the network reaches http://laptop:5173/api/v1/workflows and /metrics through the proxy.

title: Helm 'required' secrets render empty without validation
root_cause: global.encryptionKey/jwtSecret default to '' and are b64enc'd without Helm's required function; install succeeds creating empty secrets; API config loader rejects the empty/short key at boot.
suggested_fix: Use {{ required "global.encryptionKey is required" .Values.global.encryptionKey | b64enc }} (same for jwtSecret and postgres password).
failure_scenario: helm install without --set values installs 'successfully', then every API pod crash-loops on encryption-key validation — failure surfaces late and opaquely.

title: EmailNotifier stub silently succeeds without sending
root_cause: send() only logs and returns; callers receive success for an email never sent.
suggested_fix: Throw an explicit 'not implemented' error (or return failure) until SMTP lands.
failure_scenario: When the notification path is wired, email notifications no-op while workflows and the queue report success.

title: Retry sleep head-of-line-blocks the notification queue
root_cause: drain() awaits the backoff sleep (5s/30s/5min/30min) inline before processing remaining queued items; one failing item stalls everything behind it.
suggested_fix: Re-enqueue with a per-item due timestamp (or separate timers) instead of sleeping inside the drain loop.
failure_scenario: One failing webhook at the head of a 20-item queue delays all other notifications by up to 30 minutes cumulatively.

title: Recap JWT echoed into create_meeting/sync request bodies
root_cause: token resolved from input['token'] (canvas recap.sync form offers a token field); create_meeting/sync pass the whole params.input — including token — as the JSON body, duplicating the credential beyond the Authorization header.
suggested_fix: Strip token (and any auth material) from the body before JSON.stringify.
failure_scenario: JWT persisted in Recap's request-body logs in addition to the auth header, widening credential exposure on the sibling service.

title: healthCheckAll race timeout never cancels the losing probe
root_cause: Promise.race resolves false after timeoutMs but the underlying healthCheck keeps running with undici's default 300s headers/body timeout; no AbortSignal passed. /ready is unauthenticated and rate-limit-exempt (server.ts:76,333-337).
suggested_fix: Tie an AbortController to the race timeout and forward its signal into healthCheck.
failure_scenario: Repeated /ready scrapes against a blackholed sibling accumulate pending sockets (each lives up to 300s), growing memory/FD usage on the API process.

title: Non-JSON Vault /query reply silently becomes empty answer
root_cause: callVault returns {text} for any non-JSON 200 (needed for get_text raw text), so ragQuery maps answer:'' citations:[] from it. Recap added an explicit non-JSON guard for this misconfiguration class (recap/adapter.ts:124-131); Vault's /query path has none.
suggested_fix: Require JSON for /query responses (keep lenient path only for /files/{id}/text).
failure_scenario: LOOP_VAULT_URL points at a proxy serving a 200 HTML page: RAG node 'succeeds' with an empty answer instead of failing loudly; workflow continues on garbage.

title: EgressInterceptor is dead code diverging from EgressGate
root_cause: EgressInterceptor exported (index.ts:3) but never used in apps/ or packages/ (only dist typings and tests). Its request() applies only engine.evaluate — no airgap kill switch, no private-address blocklist — unlike EgressGate which all adapters actually use.
suggested_fix: Delete EgressInterceptor or make it delegate to EgressGate so the two enforcement paths cannot diverge.
failure_scenario: Developer wires EgressInterceptor.request believing it the sanctioned choke point -> outbound calls silently lose airgap and SSRF private-range protections EgressGate provides.

title: resolveIP forces IPv4; ip_range policies never match IPv6 targets
root_cause: resolveIP looks up with {family:4}; for IPv6-only hosts lookup throws and the hostname is returned, so ipInCIDR/ipToNum (engine.ts:121-144, IPv4-only) never match. ip_range allow/deny policies silently inapplicable to IPv6 literals and IPv6-only DNS names.
suggested_fix: Resolve both families and implement IPv6-aware CIDR matching (or explicitly reject ip_range evaluation for IPv6 with a logged reason).
failure_scenario: Admin adds deny ip_range for an IPv6 range and allows a domain resolving IPv6-only -> evaluate() compares hostname string against CIDR, never matches the deny; an ip_range ALLOW for IPv6 can never permit traffic, breaking intended policy.

title: CircuitBreaker never resets failure count on closed-state success
root_cause: failures only reset when a half_open probe succeeds or via reset(). Successes while closed leave the counter intact, so intermittent failures accumulate across arbitrarily long healthy periods until threshold opens the circuit against a currently-healthy service. Exported utility; not yet wired into dispatch.
suggested_fix: Reset this.failures = 0 on any successful execute() while closed (consecutive-failure semantics), or use a sliding window.
failure_scenario: threshold=5: four isolated failures spread over days (each followed by thousands of successes), then one more transient failure -> state open, all calls rejected for cooldown despite a 99.9%-healthy upstream.

title: activeRuns leaks when pre-try startup awaits throw
root_cause: this.activeRuns++ (264) happens before the try/finally that decrements it (try starts 298). If loadCompletedOutputs or store.executions.updateStatus('running') (272) throws (DB busy/IO error), the finally never runs: activeRuns stays elevated forever while metrics.activeExecutions was never incremented.
suggested_fix: Move activeRuns++ inside the try block (or wrap the whole post-increment startup sequence in the same try/finally).
failure_scenario: One transient SQLITE_BUSY during the running transition leaves activeRuns permanently >=1: every subsequent graceful shutdown's drain(10_000) waits the full 10s logging 'drain timed out' with zero in-flight work; repeated occurrences grow the counter unbounded.

title: Cancelled executions emit/record execution_failed events
root_cause: On API cancel executeInner throws EXECUTION_CANCELLED; catch calls completeExecution(...,'failed') plus recordEvent('execution_failed', reason:'node_error'). completeIfActive keeps the row 'cancelled', but the bus event type is finalStatus==='succeeded' ? succeeded : failed and the durable event unconditionally 'execution_failed'. foldExecutionEvents then reports 'failed' for a cancelled execution.
suggested_fix: When finalStatus is 'cancelled' emit a cancellation event (or skip the failure event) and record an execution_cancelled-equivalent payload.
failure_scenario: User cancels a running execution: WS monitors receive type 'execution_failed' (status 'cancelled'); event log stores execution_failed/node_error. Replay snapshot shows 'failed' while the executions row says 'cancelled' — audit trail and live view contradict the store.

title: DelayNode timer is not abortable and outlives failed executions
root_cause: DelayNode.delay uses a bare setTimeout with no AbortSignal support and no clearance. When the node/workflow timeout aborts, withTimeout rejects and the execution fails, but the delay timer keeps running (and the event loop alive) for the full requested duration.
suggested_fix: Accept an AbortSignal in DelayNode.delay, clear the timer on abort and reject; pass the fused node signal from dispatchNode.
failure_scenario: control.delay duration_ms=3600000 with default 30s node timeout: node fails at 30s, execution settles, drain() reports fully drained — yet a 1-hour timer remains pending. Embedded/SDK hosts and tests that close the store hang until it fires; shipped server survives only because main() force-exits.

title: StateMachine is dead code and contradicts actual transitions
root_cause: StateMachine exported but never invoked in production (grep-verified); stores apply transitions directly. Its tables forbid transitions the system performs: recovery running->pending (recovery.ts:54), retry/resume failed->running (executor.ts:612), replay terminal->running (executor.ts:272). Documented state machine misdescribes real behavior.
suggested_fix: Enforce transitions at the store/executor boundary (adding legitimate resume/recovery edges explicitly) or delete/annotate the module as aspirational.
failure_scenario: Developer adds a guard using StateMachine.transitionExecution for recovery: running->pending throws and crash recovery breaks — or trusts the table and assumes terminal states immutable, which replay violates.

title: Anthropic drops all but the first system message
root_cause: find() keeps only the first system message (used at line 41); LLM connector and /llm/complete accept multiple system entries; gemini.ts:38 joins them all — behavior silently differs per vendor.
suggested_fix: Join all system contents with newlines like gemini.ts:38.
failure_scenario: messages=[system A, system B, user] on Anthropic: instruction B never reaches the model; same workflow on Gemini honors both.

title: Ollama registered without default model -> router sends 'default'
root_cause: OllamaProvider always registered but LOOP_LLM_OLLAMA_MODEL optional (config.ts:84) with no fallback model; router.ts:59 substitutes the literal 'default', not a real Ollama model.
suggested_fix: Default to a common model (or discover first installed model via /api/tags) when env unset.
failure_scenario: Out of the box (local-first, no env tuning), an llm.complete node without explicit model fails with Ollama 404 "model 'default' not found".

title: CompletionRequest.stream advertised but ignored by all providers
root_cause: openai.ts:49 and ollama.ts:33 hardcode stream:false; anthropic/azure/gemini omit the field (non-streaming default). No provider honors req.stream.
suggested_fix: Remove the flag until streaming is implemented, or implement it; document the limitation either way.
failure_scenario: Caller sets stream:true expecting incremental delivery and silently receives a fully buffered response.

title: Ollama finish_reason hardcoded 'stop'; truncation invisible
root_cause: /api/chat returns done_reason ('stop'|'length'|'load') but adapter always reports 'stop'.
suggested_fix: Map data.done_reason into finish_reason.
failure_scenario: num_predict/max_tokens cuts the answer mid-sentence; downstream nodes treat truncated output as complete.

title: Ollama embed usage always 0 despite prompt_eval_count
root_cause: /api/embed responses include prompt_eval_count but adapter hardcodes usage.total_tokens=0.
suggested_fix: Read prompt_eval_count from the response into usage.total_tokens.
failure_scenario: Token accounting/budgeting under-reports all embedding usage routed through Ollama.

title: Router never calls isAvailable(); stubs return empty success
root_cause: LLMProvider.isAvailable defined and implemented by every provider but never invoked (grep-verified). bedrock.ts:16-25 and vertex.ts:15-24 return success-shaped empty completions; comments claim isAvailable=false prevents selection, untrue of this router. Latent: createLLMRouter never registers the stubs today.
suggested_fix: Skip providers whose isAvailable() resolves false (cache the probe), or make stubs throw instead of returning empty content.
failure_scenario: Future wiring registering exported BedrockProvider/VertexProvider silently produces empty answers counted as successful completions, usage 0, finish_reason 'stop'.

title: OTLP span export bypasses Egress Policy Engine; carries payload fragments
root_cause: OtlpHttpSpanExporter POSTs via global fetch directly, outside the egress gate governing all other outbound calls. Span attrs include error.message = String(err) (tracing.ts:247, executor.ts:548/229); upstream errors embed up to 200 chars of upstream response body (connectors/generic/adapter.ts:81-83) — customer data. Defaults are safe (console exporter, localhost:4318 only when opted in).
suggested_fix: Route OTLP export through the egress policy check (or document as operator-sanctioned egress); truncate/redact error.message attrs before export.
failure_scenario: Operator sets TRACE_EXPORTER=otlp OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://collector.vendor.example; a failing generic-http node puts customer response-body fragments into error.message, POSTed to the external collector without egress evaluation — contrary to the sovereignty guarantee.

title: OTLP export() throws on circular/BigInt attrs despite never-throw contract
root_cause: JSON.stringify(toOtlpJson(span)) (82) and toOtlpAnyValue's JSON.stringify(value) (116) throw TypeError on circular/BigInt attribute values; the '?? String(value)' fallback never runs because stringify throws first. exportSpan's try/catch (tracing.ts:212-219) prevents a crash but silently drops the span.
suggested_fix: Use a safe serializer (pino stdSerializers or a replacer handling cycles/BigInt) inside toOtlpJson/toOtlpAnyValue.
failure_scenario: span.setAttr('ctx', circularObject): every such span lost with only a debug log, violating the SpanExporter 'must not throw' contract for direct consumers.

title: toHex32 collapses non-hex inbound trace ids to colliding zero ids
root_cause: X-Trace-Id accepted unvalidated (middleware/traceId.ts); toHex32 strips non-hex chars then padEnd(32,'0'). Ids with no hex chars ('zzz','yyy') all become 32 zeros; >32-hex ids truncated.
suggested_fix: Hash non-conforming ids to 32 hex chars (sha256 slice) instead of zero-padding, or validate/replace the header at ingress.
failure_scenario: Clients sending X-Trace-Id 'zzz' and 'qqq' both export traceId 000...0; unrelated traces merge in the collector, trace lookups return mixed spans.

title: Sibling root spans sample independently, breaking trace-level sampling
root_cause: decideSampling inherits only from an active parent span; roots sharing the correlation trace_id each call Math.random() separately, so one trace_id can be partially exported despite the documented all-or-nothing invariant.
suggested_fix: Cache the sampling decision per trace_id (bounded LRU) and reuse for all roots of that trace.
failure_scenario: TRACE_SAMPLE_RATE=0.5: a request's API-side root span is sampled but its loop.execution root dropped (or vice versa); collector shows half-traces, trace-level debugging misleads.

title: Migration checksum stored but never verified against applied rows
root_cause: Both runners compute sha256(migration.sql) and store it, but only compare the version string against appliedSet; stored checksum never read back. Same gap in postgres/migrations.ts:29-41.
suggested_fix: On startup compare each applied migration's stored checksum to the current SQL hash; fail/warn on mismatch.
failure_scenario: Developer edits an applied migration's SQL keeping the version: runner skips it, checksum mismatch undetected, live schema drifts from code despite the checksum column existing to catch this.

title: PG workflows.delete reads execution ids outside the transaction
root_cause: SELECT id FROM workflow_executions (line 221) runs on the dedicated client BEFORE BEGIN (223). SQLite performs the equivalent read inside its transaction. An execution inserted between SELECT and DELETEs is missed by execIds.
suggested_fix: Move the SELECT inside the BEGIN...COMMIT block.
failure_scenario: New execution created after SELECT but before DELETE workflow_executions: its child rows not in execIds, DELETE hits node_executions FK -> whole transaction rolls back, delete fails.

title: SQLite workflow version bump is read-then-write; PG uses atomic version+1
root_cause: workflows.update SELECTs current.version (162) and writes version+1 computed in JS (163), not in a transaction. PG (postgres/index.ts:197) uses atomic 'version = version + 1'. Within single-process Core the synchronous better-sqlite3 block cannot interleave; only bites across processes sharing the file.
suggested_fix: Use SQL increment (version = sql`version + 1`) or wrap read+write in a transaction.
failure_scenario: Two processes sharing the SQLite file both read version N and write N+1 (lost update); duplicated version trips UNIQUE(workflow_id,version) on snapshot.

title: Registry validates only zod shape, not topology or node types
root_cause: load() runs WorkflowDefinitionSchema.safeParse but never validateWorkflow (dangling edges, cycles, duplicate ids) nor the node-type check the API applies at creation. All 30 bundled templates statically scanned clean; only bites custom LOOP_TEMPLATES_DIR content.
suggested_fix: Run validateWorkflow and known-node-type checks at load; record failures in loadErrors instead of serving unusable templates.
failure_scenario: Customer drops a template with a dangling edge into LOOP_TEMPLATES_DIR: appears in gallery but every instantiate 400s ('Invalid workflow topology') — broken surface with no load-time diagnostic.

title: Template id-collision suffix can overwrite an existing template
root_cause: On duplicate id the key is `${id}-${this.templates.size}` with no uniqueness check; the suffix can equal an id already loaded from an earlier file. Comment ('later file wins but keeps a unique key') misdescribes behavior.
suggested_fix: Loop incrementing a counter until the key is unused (while templates.has(key)).
failure_scenario: Files sorted a.json(id 'x-2'), b.json(id 'x'), c.json(id 'x'): c gets key 'x-2' (size=2), Map.set silently replaces a's template — a shipped template disappears with no load error.

title: NotFoundError cast emits error codes outside the ErrorCode union
root_cause: `NOT_FOUND_${resource.toUpperCase()}` as ErrorCode accepts any resource string. Real callers pass 'template' and 'workflow_version', producing NOT_FOUND_TEMPLATE / NOT_FOUND_WORKFLOW_VERSION which are not ErrorCode members (§12.1 envelope contract).
suggested_fix: Constrain resource to a keyof-derived union of NOT_FOUND_* codes, or add the missing codes to ErrorCode.
failure_scenario: GET /api/v1/templates/<unknown> returns NOT_FOUND_TEMPLATE; typed clients switching on ErrorCode fall through to the generic handler; contract tests against the documented enum fail.

title: Retry bounds still allow exponential backoff setTimeout overflow
root_cause: RetryConfigSchema caps max_attempts at 20 and initial_delay_ms at 60000, but exponential delay = 60000 * 2^attempt exceeds 2^31-1 from attempt 16 (~3.9e9 ms); Node fires such timers after 1ms; engine calculateBackoff has no cap.
suggested_fix: Clamp computed backoff to <= 2_147_483_647 (or a sane max like 60s) in the engine, and/or tighten schema bounds.
failure_scenario: Node with retry {max_attempts:20, initial_delay_ms:60000, backoff:'exponential'} against a persistently failing upstream: attempts 16-19 retry ~1ms apart, hammering the upstream instead of backing off.

title: Workflow update and version snapshot are non-atomic
root_cause: store.workflows.update (read-then-increment version) and versioning.createVersion run as separate operations with no transaction and no unique constraint on (workflow_id,version) (migrations create only a plain index). Concurrent definition updates can both write version N+1 and snapshot two different definitions under it; a crash between calls leaves a version with no snapshot and replay's resolveDefinition silently falls back to the live definition.
suggested_fix: Perform version bump + snapshot atomically (transaction / INSERT...RETURNING with unique (workflow_id,version) constraint); make replay's fallback explicit rather than silent.
failure_scenario: Two editors PUT different definitions simultaneously: both read version 4, both write 5, two divergent definitions snapshotted as v5. An execution stamped v5 later replays against whichever row getByWorkflowAndVersion returns first — potentially the other editor's graph.

title: Rule 5 crashes on definitions without variables; stale ref patterns
root_cause: definition.variables[varName] assumes variables present, but DB-loaded definitions are raw JSON (mapWorkflow/safeJsonParse applies no zod defaults), so a stored definition lacking variables throws TypeError inside validateWorkflow. Accepted patterns out of sync with executor: variables.* and raw-node-id references ({{fetch.output.x}}, hyphenated ids) valid at runtime but flagged 'may not resolve'; variables.foo looked up as literal key instead of stripping the prefix.
suggested_fix: Use (definition.variables ?? {})[...], strip the variables. prefix before lookup, accept the executor's reference grammar (trigger.payload.*, variables.*, any <nodeId>.output.*).
failure_scenario: POST /api/v1/workflows/:id/validate on a legacy/imported row without variables key and config containing {{variables.recipient}} -> TypeError -> 500; on current rows valid {{variables.x}}/{{fetch.output.y}} references produce spurious warnings.

title: Flagship scenario 'triggers via webhook' never fires the webhook handler
root_cause: A webhook trigger row is created (47-54) but never used; the execution record is hand-inserted with trigger_type 'webhook' and driven directly by ctx.executor. Comment 56-59 ('executor not yet wired to auto-run from triggers') is stale — routes/index.ts:596-611 dispatches webhook executions. Title overstates coverage.
suggested_fix: Fire the real webhook handler (HMAC-signed inject like trigger-to-execution.test.ts) or rename/recomment and delete the unused trigger.
failure_scenario: Readers believe the flagship webhook->execution pipeline is E2E-covered here; a webhook-dispatch regression is only caught by the integration suite; stale comment misdirects maintainers.

title: buildTestApp temp dirs and git repos are never cleaned up
root_cause: Every buildTestApp call mkdtempSync's a loop-test-* dir (DB + git repo); test files close app/conn but nothing removes the directory. auth-guard/rbac/replay build one app per test, leaking dozens of dirs per run. e2e/helpers.ts:146-153 does rmSync correctly — divergent cleanup discipline.
suggested_fix: Expose close() on TestApp that closes conn and rmSync(tmpDataDir,{recursive:true,force:true}); use in afterAll (or track dirs in tests/setup.ts afterEach).
failure_scenario: CI workers and dev machines accumulate orphaned SQLite files and git repos in os.tmpdir() across runs; disk pressure on long-lived self-hosted CI runners.

title: Unused THREE_NODE_DEFINITION references unimplemented desk.create_task
root_cause: Exported but referenced nowhere in the test tree. Uses desk.create_task which the real DeskAdapter does not implement (connectors/desk.test.ts:126 asserts its absence). STUB_THREE_NODE is copy-pasted divergently in api/executions.test.ts:20-48 and engine/e2e-execution.test.ts:22-50.
suggested_fix: Delete THREE_NODE_DEFINITION or rebuild on implemented operations (desk.send_response); hoist the shared stub into _helpers/app.ts.
failure_scenario: Maintainer picks the 'official' helper definition for a new E2E test and gets a confusing execution-time failure instead of a working fixture.

title: Egress CRUD test claims cache invalidation but never asserts its effect
root_cause: Title says 'round-trips and invalidates the cache' yet only checks HTTP CRUD responses; never evaluates ctx.egressEngine before/after create/update/delete to prove invalidateCache() took effect (route calls it at routes/index.ts:694,711,718).
suggested_fix: After creating an allow policy via POST, assert ctx.egressEngine.evaluate flips denied->allowed without manual invalidateCache; after DELETE assert it flips back.
failure_scenario: Dropping deps.egressEngine.invalidateCache() from the policy routes leaves stale cached policies in production (new deny rules ignored until TTL) while this test stays green.

title: WS tests use a private executor+bus pair, not production singleton wiring
root_cause: Both describes build a fresh ExecutionExecutor with a dedicated EventBus and register the WS route with that bus (also 175-181). Production relies on the process-wide executionEventBus shared by executor default and registerExecutionWebSocket (server.ts:229-231,328). Deliberate per comment, but actual production wiring is never asserted.
suggested_fix: Add one test using ctx.executor (default singleton bus) with registerExecutionWebSocket(app,{eventBus:executionEventBus}) from the same module graph.
failure_scenario: A server.ts change passing a different bus instance to the WS route than the executor publishes to breaks live monitoring in production while this suite stays green.

title: undici mock (always 200, no body) hides notifier's missing status check
root_cause: Mock returns {statusCode:200} with no body. WebhookNotifier.send ignores statusCode and never consumes response.body (socket leak); a downstream 500 resolves as success so NotificationQueue would never retry. Mock cannot express non-2xx or a body. Notifier classes currently unwired, hence Low.
suggested_fix: Mock full response ({statusCode, body:{text:async()=>''}}); add non-2xx case asserting send() rejects; consume body in notifier; add NotificationQueue retry test with fake timers.
failure_scenario: Once wired, a downstream outage (500) silently treated as delivered and the retry queue never engages; HMAC-only test stays green.

title: Public-hostname assertions do real DNS and are vacuous when DNS fails
root_cause: firstPrivateAddress returns null on DNS failure; tests assert null/allow for https://example.com. Offline or with broken DNS the same assertions pass without resolution, unable to distinguish 'resolved public' from 'resolution broken (fail-open)'. Also makes the unit suite network-dependent.
suggested_fix: Mock node:dns (correct {all:true} array shape) for public-hostname cases; keep literal-IP cases real; reserve real-DNS localhost coverage for one explicitly marked test.
failure_scenario: Regression making lookupAll always throw disables hostname-based private blocking; these tests still pass offline; flaky network dependence masks the difference in CI.

title: Dead fixture code and wrong retry-semantics comment mislead readers
